name: 1099 String Quartet - Late Beethoven Quartets at Wicker

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: Treat yourself to the 1099 String Quartet (Professional Ensemble) performing LIVE at Wicker Park! This year, the quartet led by Ryan Loeckel (Artistic Director) will present 3 of the Late Beethoven String Quartets: String Quartet No. 14 in C sharp minor, Op. 131 (1826) (Performed 6/25 at 11am), String Quartet No. 15 in A minor, Op. 132 (1825) (Performed 8/6 at 11am), String Quartet No. 16 in F major, Op. 135 (1826) (Performed 8/27 at 11am). Ryan Loeckel will give both musical and historic notes on the music performed. Bring a Blanket and Picnic. Performer BIOS & Details: www.WickerPark.org

name: 2 Day: South Side Skating Academy at Morgan Park SC

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: The South Side Skating Academy is a Bridge Program, for skaters looking to Bridge the gap between recreational Learn to Skate, and starting to become a competitive skater. The Academy is for skaters in Pre-Free Skate through Free Skate 3, and is made up of multiple classes (on and off the ice) each week, for a reduced rate. Skaters in the Bridge Program will be enrolled in this structured training program, with the goal to join the MPSC Competitive Team. Cost (if registered for 2 more sessions) also includes a Membership Team Jacket, and other activities.

name: 2027 Herbie Hancock Fellows at Marquette

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: Join the Marquette Park Cultural Center for a free concert! In fall 2025, six extraordinary young jazz musicians from around the world were selected for the Herbie Hancock Institute of Jazz Performance at UCLA, Class of 2027. These excellent players study deeply as individuals and as a small group—receiving personal mentoring, ensemble coaching, and lectures on the jazz tradition from the legends of the jazz tradition. Beyond that, they are charged to experiment in expanding jazz in new directions through their compositions and performances. Herbie Hancock Fellows have performed in Saint Petersburg, Russia; Havana, Cuba; Melbourne, Sydney and Mt. Gambier, Australia; at the celebration commemorating the 40th anniversary of the coronation of the King of Thailand, the 1998 Summit of the Americas in Chile before 34 heads of state, the United Nations “Day of Philosophy” event in Paris sponsored by UNESCO, and the Tokyo Jazz Festival. The students have also participated in tours of Argentina, China, Egypt, India, Morocco, Peru, Russia, Vietnam and, most recently, Jordan with Institute Chairman Herbie Hancock. These musicians’ concepts and playing will come to define the sound of jazz well into the future. Come get an early glimpse into what that jazz will sound like. The Hancock Fellows will come to the Marquette Park Cultural Center on April 28th at 4:30 for a free show in its historic auditorium. This unprecedented performance has come to the Southwest Side as a part of International Jazz Day celebrations, hosted this year by the City of Chicago. Free admission! Nicolaus Gelin: trumpet Nathan Gilbreath: trombone Mwanzi Harriott: guitar Yerin Kim: bass Elisee Ngbo: piano Mailo Rakotonanahary: drums

name: 312 Grit at Jefferson

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 12 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: 312 Grit is a functional fitness and personal development program designed for individuals who aspire to elevate their health, performance, and overall quality of life. The program integrates high-level functional training with education in proper nutrition and intentional character development, creating a well-rounded approach to long-term success. At its core, 312 Grit focuses on improving sports performance, strength, conditioning, mobility, and resilience through purposeful, scalable workouts. Beyond physical training, participants are guided in building sustainable nutrition habits that support performance, recovery, and lifelong wellness. What sets 312 Grit apart is its emphasis on developing the character traits of tomorrow’s leaders: discipline, accountability, grit, teamwork, and integrity. Through mentorship, structured competition, and shared challenges, athletes learn to push beyond comfort while supporting one another in a team-centered environment. 312 Grit is more than a workout class; it is a mentoring-driven community where individuals are challenged to grow physically, mentally, and emotionally. The program prepares participants not only to perform at a higher level in sport, but to lead with confidence, resilience, and purpose in every area of life.

name: A Place to Play Summit at South Shore

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: The Sport for Good Chicago coalition has partnered with the Chicago Park District to host “A Place to Play” – a one-day summit discussing the role that public space activation plays in building a safer city. During this day, stakeholders across the city will have a chance to learn from expert researchers and practitioners, exchange success stories, and work with one another to explore the unique power we all have in moving this work forward. This event is for visionary leaders who are committed to imagining a city where young people and their families are able to use their public spaces to sustain a strong community, move their bodies and feel safe to play. You have been invited to this event because you play a role in bringing that vision to life. We hope to see you there.

name: AACM Future Explorations at Fred Anderson

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: This year the AACM would like to celebrate the future of our Great Black Music tradition, ancient to the future. We will feature compositions from three of our youngest members- Adam Zanolini, Alexis Lombre, and Angel Bat Dawid. Their development as musicians and composers has been nurtured by the inter-generational ensemble of the AACM's Great Black Music Ensemble. These three emerging composers draw upon traditional forms of African American music and music from the African diaspora. These musicians push boldly into radically unknown territory, creating future explorations of the outer realms. This event is presented as a part of the City of Chicago’s 2020 Year of Chicago Music. Experience music in the key of Chicago at www.YearofChicagoMusic.org .

name: About Face Theatre Pres. Life Out Loud at Gill

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: Three friends journey through a gallery of stories from LGBTQ+ people, past and present. Together they investigate history’s torn out pages, discovering the power of authentic friendship, and new ideas to expand our understanding of gender and sexuality. This charming, funny, and interactive play uses poetry and improv to introduce gender expansive vocabulary, healthy coping mechanisms and often forgotten Black and Asian queer history. Starring Haven A.J. Crawley, Jett Pasia, and Ua Smith. Written by Dionne Addai, with the Life Out Loud Ensemble and Theatrical Consultation from Lexi Saunders including contributed pieces from Zahra Baker and Aimy Tien.

name: Adaptive Goal Ball at Horner

age_range.raw_age_text: 12 yrs +

description: For individuals whose primary disability is visual impairment.. Goal Ball is played in a gymnasium with two teams with three people on each team. Each team stands at opposing ends of the gym. The object is to throw a ball, which is similar to a basketball, past the other team. The ball has bells on the inside, so the teams can hear when the ball is coming. Players will learn the basic skills, rules and fundamentals of the game.

name: Adaptive Goalball (Blind-VI) at Horner

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: For individuals with a primary visual impairment. Goalball is a team sport designed for athletes with a visual impairment. Participants will compete in teams of three and try to throw a ball that has bells embedded in it into their opponent's goal. Players will learn the basic skills, rules and fundamentals of the game.

name: Adult Martial Arts & Self Defense at Morgan Park SC

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Our Martial Arts program will build on the skills that focuses on the self-defense and Kung Fu. The curriculum includes conflict resolution and non-lethal restraint. Skills include blocks, kicks, punches, falls and throws. All students receive a study sheet that will assist parents in reviewing the material. The class also works on flexibility, running, endurance, strength, concentration and coordination. Students will perform exercises such as jogging, jumping jacks, lunges, and push ups. All students will begin with a warmup; if student is tardy, they will still have a quick warmup to prepare their body for class activity. Participants are able to sign up for more than one class for additional practice and develop stronger technique

name: Adult Modern Partnership at Berger

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Kristina Fluty leads this modern dance class for advanced and professional dancers, hosted by Arts Partner Synapse Arts. Kristina has been teaching and dancing in Chicago for the past two decades. Her main creative home since 2003 is molly Shanahan/Mad Shak, and she is currently completing the inaugural Spiral Body Techniques teacher certification with Shanahan. She is an Associate Professor at The Theatre School at DePaul, where she teaches movement to actors. Her dance class prioritizes pleasure and honoring/embracing how you move right now. It is also anchored by Fluty's certification in Laban/Bartenieff Movement Analysis and her many years of Feldenkrais personal study. Class will likely begin on the floor with gentle developmental movement phases, then evolve out into dancing with delicious complexity, spatial clarity, and ease.

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Join us for an evening of recreation, wellness, and connection at our Adult Sports & Social Night! Whether you're looking to stay active, learn a new sport, or simply enjoy time with friends, this program offers something for everyone. Participants will rotate through a variety of activities, including ice skating, tennis, and pickleball, with opportunities for all skill levels to participate in a fun and welcoming environment. The evening also includes a wellness session focused on stretching, recovery, mindfulness, or healthy living to help promote overall well-being. Come meet new people, enjoy friendly competition, and experience a balanced night of fitness, fun, and community.

name: Adult Swimming and Sports (Special Rec) at Mt. Greenwood

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: For individuals with a primary intellectual or developmental disability. Participants will learn basic swimming techniques, advanced breathing techniques, and mechanics of the four basic strokes (freestyle, backstroke, butterfly and breaststroke). Participants will be grouped according to skill level. Learn to play a variety of sports and brush up on skills. Instructors teach and reinforce skills development through drills and game play, with a concentration on sportsmanship and friendly competition. Sports vary by season.

name: Adult Wheelchair Basketball at Jesse White

age_range.raw_age_text: 15 yrs +

description: For individuals with a primary physical disability. The Chicago Skyhawks are a partnership with the Shirley Ryan AbilityLab (SRALab) and the Chicago Park District for individuals with a primary physical disability to play the amazing game of wheelchair basketball. Through individual and team drills athletes will raise their level of play and gain an understanding of the game. The Skyhawks compete in the National Wheelchair Basketball Association (NWBA) Division III at regional tournaments and events. Indoor wheelchair softball practice will begin on April 9th.

name: Adult Wheelchair Softball at California

age_range.raw_age_text: 14 yrs +

description: Wheelchair Softball is one of the premier sport choices for members of Chicago's adaptive sports community. The program is for people with a primary physical disability to come out and take part in Chicago's sport of choice at Cubs Care Field at California Park; which was one of the first fields in the United States designed for play in the National Wheelchair Softball Association (NWSA). Currently there are two teams of athletes in the program who compete in tournaments throughout the area and if they qualify will move onto the national tournament. For more information please contact Special Recreation Adaptive Sport Program & Event Coordinator Daniel Ferreira for more information: daniel.ferreira@chicagoparkdistrict.com

name: Afro-Caribbean Maypole: Woven Culture at Columbus

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: This event has been canceled due to weather. We look forward to rescheduling on another date.Through dance and rooted rhythms, A 3D Canvas of Woven Culture will take you into a merry-go-round of weaving and unweaving, circling and uncircling, braiding and unbraiding the colors and history of Afro-Caribbean and European exchange through the Maypole dance. You will be invited to dance and wrap to lively Afro-Caribbean drumming and song. The activity will be circled by dance, song, and music representing many of the Afro-Caribbean islands... get a glimpse of the unique performance art traditions. Perhaps it'll help you decide your next vacation. Wherever you go, don't forget your ribbon to show them" what you've got .... trained and true by the West Indian Dance Theater Company of Chicago! https://www.facebook.com/WIDTC

name: AfroSoul Yoga Drum Circle at Euclid

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: A two part event starting with an all inclusive drum circle. The Drum Circle leader gives a brief history on the Djembe, then leads participants through basic rhythms they can play during the dance portion of the event. The 2nd portion is an invigorating, fun for all ages, DANCE focused YOGA. Lively sounds of drums and soul stirring BASS, participants will "DANCE YOUR WAY TO NAMASTE"™? with movements from across the African Diaspora. As an active meditation, all the principles and intention of yoga are the foundation. The dance portion is not about learning the dances to proficiency but using the repetitive movement, freeing your mind and using the breath work needed to execute the various combos to achieve your yoga. In accordance with Be Safe Chicago Guidelines for Parks and Recreation Activities, participants in this activity will be required to wear a mask and practice social distancing at all times while participating. Patrons who are exhibiting any symptoms of COVID-19 are asked to stay home and join us for an event when symptoms subside.

name: Ahimsa: The End of Violence at Dawes

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: “Ahimsa: The End of Violence” presents three classical tales from around the world (Ancient Greece, 19th Century America, and ancient India), narrated and told through classical Indian Bharatanatyam dance to original music compositions. The theme of these tales centers around the futility of violence and the triumph of peace. South Asian American Policy and Research Institute (SAAPRI) will work with Kalapriya again to coordinate a panel of community leaders/activists to hold panel discussions on the themes of "Ahimsa" and productive solutions and responses to violence within the community. The programs will end with audience input and a community dance.

name: AIKYAM // MOSAIC at Arrigo

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: Alex in Windyland is a new play about the complexities of the foster care system. The day before her 12th birthday, Alex is taken from her sister and transported onto a train called Windyland. Windyland is a magical liminal space where Alex faces new challenges, finds new friends, and goes on adventures. Will Alex be reunited with her sister? Will she find a forever home? The clock is ticking, and the train keeps running. As the train speeds forward, the urgency of her situation becomes clear, just as it does for thousands of foster youth navigating an unpredictable system.

name: America: Songs of Protest and Freedom at Clarendon

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: 2026 marks the 250th anniversary of the United States. America: Songs and Stories of Protest and Freedom is a multi-genre concert of spoken word and music. It’s written and narrated by award-winning journalist, Cheryl Corley, and features a stellar band lead by singer/songwriter Lucy Smith. The concert chronicles America’s story from its founding years to the 21st century. It includes Walt Whitman’s “I Hear America Singing” along with the words of other American authors. Songs include: Curtis Mayfield’s “This is My Country”, John Lennon’s “Imagine,” and Beyonce’s “Freedom.” It is a performance that presents the intricacies of America’s 250 years.

description: American Choral Classics celebrates the richness and range of the American choral tradition, bringing together music by a wonderfully diverse group of American composers. Spanning poetry, folk song, spirituals, protest, and hymn-inspired reflection, the program explores the many voices that shape America’s musical identity, personal and communal, searching and joyful, deeply rooted and always evolving. name: An Autumnal Celebration at McKinley

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: A medley of singing, dancing, a fashion show, and other forms of performing arts will be staged to celebrate, in the traditionally oriental way, the family-reuniting festival, one of the grandest festivities honored throughout Asian countries. As this is our first effort to reach a park where most visitors are said to be Spanish-speaking, we are to incorporate Mexican and Black elements of culture and arts into our performance by inviting artists of multi-ethnic origins and putting up shows of multiple languages. www.chicagochineseculture.com

name: An Introduction to Shamanism at McFetridge

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Meet Your Power Animal & Learn to Journey: An Introduction to Shamanism Introduce yourself to modern Shamanism and its worldwide origins; A way of life combining earthly traditions and spiritual practices teaching us to walk in both worlds. Learn the basic skills of the meditative practice known as Shamanic Journeying: - Create a Sacred Circle - Meet your Power Animal - This Spirit Guide may be a new surprise or an old friend - Journey together to non-ordinary reality - Connect more deeply to Spirit to receive Divine Guidance - Acknowledge your true self and her/his needs - Access information to help you unlock healing relief on many levels By bringing the teachings of shamanism into our daily lives, we can more fully experience our own Divinity, our innate connection to the web of life and dream a new dream for ourselves and the world. Awaken knowledge from deep within you to support "remembering" the Journey of Our Soul. What to bring: Wear comfortable clothing since meditations can be seated or lying down as well as a special blanket or sheet to be on/wrap yourself in and an eye covering (mask or scarf) to help you create a sacred focused space. Other things to bring if you?re called are something sacred to place on the altar, a journal to jot down your insights, a hand drum, or rattle. Please let me know ahead of time if you have a breathing issue which would prevent a smoke smudge since we have an easy alternative. Questions? Contact Monica at (773) 310-1228 or MonicaMoonPlace@gmail.com *Class will be cancelled if 3 participant minimum is not met 3 days prior*

name: Anatomical Circus at Sherman

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: Chicago Rewilding Society presents "'Anatomical Circus", an installation of life-size anatomical educational dioramas, anatomical face painting, and animal-assisted therapy with fantastically painted creatures. Anatomical Circus explores our internal and external landscapes, invigorating audiences to celebrate and understand their own humanness through wonder, delight & a sense of magic.

name: Anchor Curatorial Residency Info Session at Ellis

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: Join us for an Anchor Curatorial Residency Info Session at Ellis Park to learn more about the residency, meet the park staff, and ask questions. To learn more or to apply to be the 2026-2027 Anchor Curator-in-Residence, please visit this site.

name: Anchor Residency Welcome Reception at Ellis

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: We invite you to celebrate and meet Lional "Brother El" Freeman at the Anchor Residency Curator Welcome Reception at Ellis Park on Thursday, May 21, from 5:30 to 7:30 pm. Starting at 5:30 pm, you’ll have the chance to mingle with the curator, enjoy local bites from Carver 47, and connect with fellow community members. The evening will culminate with a panel at 6:00 pm featuring past and present Anchor collaborators, and we’ll have the grand debut of our Anchor Monograph! RSVP for event through this link . This monograph, which was published at the end of last year, is now ready to make its way out into the world for you, dear readers. It builds on the success of previous residencies at Austin Town Hall Park and Marquette Park. In partnership with Sixty Inches From Center, an online art publication, the publication critically engages with the residency’s learnings and outcomes, highlighting how municipalities can empower culture workers to address community harm through public/private partnerships. Supported by a grant from the Terra Foundation in 2024 and additional support from the Builder’s Initiative, the monograph was edited by multidisciplinary artist Kamilah Rashied. Anchor Curatorial Residency is a funded Chicago Park District community-driven curatorial residency that rotates among the Chicago Park District’s Cultural Centers. ** About Lional "Brother El" Freeman Brother El is a Chicago-based social practice artist, spontaneous composer, audio engineer, and educator whose work bridges music, community engagement, and public space. Rooted in hip-hop, DIY culture, and South Side Chicago, he is known for his improvised Live PA performances using drum machines, samplers, and synthesizers. He also founded The Beat Bank and creates dynamic public art events, such as Sandbox Symphony, transforming spaces into vibrant, community-centered cultural hubs. Through his work, Brother El expands access to art, uplifts youth and artist communities, and inspires creative possibility. We can’t wait to see his vision come to life at Ellis Park!

name: Angel Bat Dawid at Jackson Park

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: The Art Institute of Chicago presents a performance by Chicago clarinetist and composer Angel Bat Dawid in Jackson Park. Bat Dawid performs her original five-movement suite titled Peace: A Suite for Sky Landing, a Mended Petal Odyssey, composed in response to Yoko Ono’s Skylanding. Bat Dawid performs with the Cosmic Space Arkestra. This event is presented as a part of the City of Chicago’s 2020 Year of Chicago Music. Experience music in the key of Chicago at www.YearofChicagoMusic.org .

description: Join the Chicago Public Library, Vodak-East Side Branch at Big Marsh Park for a 30-minute nature-inspired story time directly followed by a 30-minute complementary activity. Activities could include meeting an animal, going on a nature hike, and exploring loose parts and sensory stations. This program is open to all youth and families. Registration is encouraged; walk-ins are welcome. Come early or stay late to explore the nearly 300-acre Natural Area and Bike Park that is Big Marsh Park.

name: Annual Bike Rally at The 606

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: The Third Annual 606 Bike Rally is a collaboration with the Chicago Police Department's 14th and 25th Districts, West Town Bikes and other local community organizations. The rally is a fun, free event that engages and encourages bicycle riders of all ages and abilities. Bike-focused resource partners set up at both the east and west ends of The 606 and provide a wide range of free resources: everything from healthy snacks, tune-ups, quick tutorials, helmet fittings, light and bike bell giveaways, and bike maps and guides are all available. Adding to the festive spirit of the event are bike decorating stations, obstacle courses, a bike washing area and live music from local school bands. This event is free and open to the public.

name: Annual Plant Sale at Kilbourn

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: The 28th Annual Plant Sale will be held in-person at the Kilbourn Park Greenhouse. You can view the list of plants here. Kilbourn Park Greenhouse will offer more than 150 varieties of organically-grown vegetable, herb, edible flower seedlings and so much more. Customers can expect a wide variety of open-pollinated and heirloom tomatoes, peppers, and eggplants. Other highlights include an assortment of herbs, greens and onions. These seedlings are grown with the support of a team of dedicated volunteers who make this Plant Sale possible. Volunteers will be on hand to answer questions about plant selection and planting. This yearly fundraiser supports the greenhouse and our work to connect kids to nature and healthy foods. Also available at the plant sale: Perennials and other plants donated by volunteers of the Kilbourn Park Organic Greenhouse, compost, and bake sale items. Look for the Friends of Kilbourn Park Organic Greenhouse tables just outside the main gate to the gardens. Cost: Free Admission, Plant Prices $4. | cash and credit accepted. We suggest that you bring a box or some type container to carry your purchases.

Participants move at a slow pace in this low to moderate intensity activity, while doing less intense exercises in chest deep water. The aquatic environment is easy on the joints and offers more resistance. General activity format includes a warm up, cardio work, strengthening work and cool down. No swimming experience needed.

name: AARP Smart Driver Course

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Co-sponsored by the AARP and Naperville Park District, this program (formerly known as the AARP Driver Safety Program) is a comprehensive driver-retraining course geared to the specific needs of older motorists. Learn the effects of aging and medications on driving, basic driving rules, license renewal procedures, local traffic hazards and more. Designed to improve your driving abilities through additional training, attention and practice, this two-day course helps you drive more safely and keep your driver's license longer. Most auto insurance companies offer a discount for people who attend this class. Call your local insurance agent for more details. The fee is $25 ($20 for AARP card-carrying members). Fees are subject to change. Payment goes directly to instructor. Make checks payable to AARP. Cash is not accepted. Although it is free to book a spot in the class, there is a fee for this program. (jg)

name: Adult Hike with a Naturalist

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

location: Street Parking on Azalea Ct. or Feldott Lane
description: Join a naturalist on a morning hike around the pond at Wildflower Park on Aurora Ave. The entire trail is paved and level. Bring a water bottle and wear sturdy walking shoes. Please note: Street parking on Azalea Ct or Feldott Lane. A map showing these streets and the meeting location will be emailed to participants 3 days before the hike. No restrooms at this park. (ah)

name: Advanced Pottery and Sculpture

price.raw_price_text: Resident: $172.00; Non-resident: $202.00; Senior, 60 and over, resident: $137.60; Senior, 60 and over, non-resident: $161.60

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Challenge your hand-building and surface decorating skills in a relaxed studio atmosphere with individual guidance provided based on individual needs and requests. Class work explores unity of form and surface treatment with more complex forms using texture, color, scale and series of objects. Although the class title is "Advanced", only a beginning level of clay work and familiarity with the studio is required. Your inspiration may start with Pinterest, but you will leave the class with art that is uniquely yours. Bring your inspiration, sense of humor and desire to explore your creativity in an environment that fosters personal growth. Each participant receives an individual space to store work. All supplies are included. Prerequisite: participation in a previous Naperville Park District pottery class. No class June 29 & July 6. (bd)

name: Adventure Camp Grades: 1-5

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: Adventure Camp is all about discovering new friendships, enjoying arts and crafts, playing lots of group games and participating in individual and team sports. On the first two Thursdays of the session, camp will travel to Centennial Beach and then on the last Thursday of the session, we'll take a field trip to a fun destination! On Thursdays, campers begin the day at 8:45 a.m. with pick up at 3:00 p.m. Campers need to bring a snack, drink and lunch each day. Fee includes Adventure Camp T-shirt to wear on field trip days. Detailed information about camp is located at www.napervilleparks.org/camps (dn)

name: Ageless Grace®: Timeless Fit for the Body and Mind

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Welcome to Ageless Grace®: Timeless Fit for the Body and Mind, a cutting-edge brain fitness program based on neuroplasticity that activates all five functions of the brain-strategic planning, memory/recall, analytical thinking, creativity and imagination and kinesthetic learning while simultaneously addressing all 21 physical skills needed for lifelong optimal function. This unique program works for all ages and all fitness and ability levels. Instructor Cecilia Floyd-Carruthers will teach you the 21 Tools that focus on different anti-aging techniques like Shake It Up Baby, Dance Party, Spaghetti Spine and more, all set to lively and familiar music. Just imagine all of this plus tons of laughter. Stretch, bend and strengthen your core muscles while adding the twist of cognitive learning to build those brain cells. This program works by providing increased stability while seated in a chair! It's time to add fun to exercise and experience the newest way to move both mind and body. Please note that this class is done barefoot while sitting in a chair. Bring comfy socks if needed. (jg)

name: All-Star Baseball Skills

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 10 yrs

description: Kids learn the importance of proper throwing mechanics, rotational hitting, bunting, fielding, pitching and catching. Speed and agility techniques are added to increase core strength and mobility for added bat speed, range in the field and linear speed for base running. In-game strategies are included to increase each player's overall knowledge. Led by All Star Sports Instruction, Inc. (sa)

name: All-Star Basketball Juniors

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 7 yrs

description: Fun basketball-like games are played to teach the importance of each skill learned.The foundation technique focuses on basic mechanics to build confidence and then adds larger challenges. Footwork is an extremely important aspect of the game; no player sits! We also work on dribbling with each hand, passing and shooting and understanding basic offense and defense in addition to learning teamwork and sportsmanship. Taught by All Star Sports. (sa)

name: All-Star Basketball Skills

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 10 yrs

description: Trainers focus on individual skills as well as team play. Each class begins with speed and agility drills to enhance each player's ability to get up and down the court quickly, generate rapid change of direction and create explosion to the basket. Ball handling, proper shooting technique, footwork and defensive/offensive strategies also are included. Small-sided competitions and game play enable each player to focus and work on skills learned. Led by All Star Sports Instruction, Inc. (sa)

name: All-Star Parent-Tot Sports

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 5 yrs

description: Enjoy this opportunity to bond and have fun together while learning a variety of sports. Program offers a great opportunity to improve the simple motor skills of catching, throwing, batting, shooting, passing, running and also improve developing hand-eye coordination. Parents participate with the child playing soccer, basketball, hockey, T-Ball, football and other sports. Led by All Star Sports Instruction, Inc. (sa)

name: All-Star Soccer Juniors

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 7 yrs

description: Keep kids active and engaged both mentally and physically in this great base to prepare them for the next level of play. Soccer is a game that is action-packed so there's no sitting and waiting! The game of soccer is learned by hiding drills in fun games and using association techniques. Simple foot skills, dribbling, passing, shooting, basic rules and even work on spreading the field are covered. Kids also learn teamwork and sportsmanship. Led by All Star Sports Instruction, Inc. (sa)

name: All-Star Soccer Skills

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 10 yrs

description: This program includes speed and agility drills to improve each player's soccer game by allowing for a more powerful shot, increased range on the field and efficient change of direction. Basic skills of dribbling, shooting passing and spacing are covered and expanded upon. Players learn the importance of movement away from the ball and the importance of each position through game situations. Taught by All Stars Sports Instruction, Inc. (sa)

name: All-Star Super Sports Juniors

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 5 yrs

description: Designed for the all-around athlete or the child who wants to take a shot at different sports. Kids stay active and work on balance, motor skills and hand-eye coordination while learning the rules of baseball, football, floor hockey, soccer, basketball and more! Each class focuses on a new sport, basic rules and mechanics while games are played that keep everyone moving. Led by All Star Sports Instruction, Inc. (sa)

name: All-Star T-Ball Juniors

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 7 yrs

description: T-Ball can be a boring game if taught incorrectly. This approach to baseball is one that engages players regardless of skill level. They learn basic building blocks in a fun, safe environment. Program keeps players moving and learning even while in the dugout! Mechanics and hand-eye coordination are the keys to early success. Players gain confidence as they learn the proper mechanics of catching, throwing, fielding, base-running and batting. This fun, exciting program prepares each player for the Level II, T-Ball or Coach Pitch leagues. Taught by All Star Sports Instruction, Inc. (sa)

name: Aquatic Fitness

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: Tone muscles and increase cardiovascular fitness through various exercises while using the natural resistance and buoyancy of water. Swimming ability is not required. Ann Jansen will be the instructor for this class. For weather-related cancellations, please visit www.napervilleparks.org. (cj)

name: Archery

age_range.raw_age_text: 9 yrs +

description: Expert instruction in this Olympic sport is provided by a team of National Archery Association-certified instructors who teach target archery in a fun and safe environment. All instruction follows the Junior Olympic Archery Development program guidelines of the NAA. Tight-fitting clothing or short-sleeved shirts are recommended. All equipment is provided; please do not bring or buy any gear. Fee is per person. (fg)

name: Baby Rock

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3m but less than 1y 4m

description: Wiggle and giggle with Baby Rock! This program is a unique combination of sensory experiences with stimulating music and exercises to help strengthen and stretch your baby. Activities will include sing-alongs, exposure to simple instruments and sensory props, bean bag massages, motion exercises, bubbles, and more! Please bring a blanket or mat and get ready for a rockin' good time with your tiniest dancer! (sl)

name: Balance, Breath and Movement (hybrid)

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Balance, Breath and Movement focus on functional movement for daily life. Exercises are drawn from Chinese Qi Gongs and Tai Chi movements that work on balance and flexibility, as well as breathing techniques, to enhance the movements and relieve stress. All can be done seated if needed. (jg)

name: Ballet Basics

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: Looking to enter the world of ballet? Younger and beginning dancers are able to explore dance and expand their ballet knowledge in this program focused on classroom etiquette, posture, ballet terminology and intricate positions of the feet, arms and body in a creative and expressive environment. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: Ballet/Tap Basics

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: This program is designed to build a solid dance foundation. Dancers learn proper posture and technique while being introduced to dance terminology from both dance styles. The program focuses on the fundamentals of ballet technique, incorporating tap to help with rhythm, tempo and distribution of weight. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: Ballet: Adult Beginner

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Learn the fundamentals of ballet while lengthening and strengthening your body and increasing your flexibility. This program is perfect for students new to ballet or those looking to return to the art. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: Ballet: Junior

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 7 yrs

description: Dancers begin their ballet training learning basic ballet exercises while incorporating musicality and rhythm and focusing on classroom etiquette, posture, ballet terminology and positions of the feet, arms and body. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: Ballet: Level 1

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 10 yrs

description: This program incorporates basic barre exercises and center work focusing on arm and head coordination, rhythm, correct body alignment, change of direction and poise. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: Ballet: Level 2 & 3

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 9 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: Dancers begin learning petit allegro movements in the center and continue to focus on the ballet skills begun at previous levels. The correct execution of steps is encouraged and more difficult combinations are taught. ***Prerequisite of the previous level or equivalent experience is required. For questions on placement, please contact the Dance Coordinator at 630-848-3618. *** Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: Basketball Camps:

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Learn basketball fundamentals using drills, scrimmages and contests. Players are grouped by ability when numbers permit. (fg)

name: Before Camp at Camp Frontier

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: Available to all of the registered early risers attending Camp Frontier. (dn)

name: Before Camp at Camp Seager

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: Available to all of the registered early risers attending Camp Seager. (dn)

name: Bingo

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Bring your friends, or come alone and make some new ones! Event includes snack and a beverage, 12 games of regular bingo, and if you're lucky, prizes! Deadline to register is the Monday before each bingo event. (jg)

name: Boom! Kids Art Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 10 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: When artistic ideas explode, who knows what students will come up with! Create art using markers, pencils, paint, chalk, glitter, sticks, scrap wood, shells, cardboard, hot glue and more. We will take material donations such as corks, happy meal toys, string, etc. Participants should also bring a lunch, snacks and something to drink. Supply fee of $40 is due to the instructor at the first class. (bd)

name: Camp Frontier

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 9 yrs

description: This full-day, week-long camp keeps kids having fun all summer! They'll discover new friendships, enjoy arts and crafts, play group games and participate in individual and team sports. Camp will travel to Centennial Beach twice a week to swim and take a field trip to a fun destination once each week. Campers need to bring their lunch each day except Wednesday when a pizza, chips and lemonade lunch is provided. Fee includes Camp Frontier T-shirt to wear on field trip days. Early pickup is available at 3:00 p.m. each day except Friday field trip days. Registration numbers for day camps are closed on the Wednesday of the week prior to camp. Registrations for day camps are accepted only up to a determined maximum number. Closing of registrations for day camp is being implemented in order for the Park District to monitor camp enrollment and ensure proper staffing levels. All detailed information about camp is located at www.napervilleparks.org/camps. Early drop off is available at 7:00 a.m. to all of the registered early risers attending Camp Frontier. (dn)

name: Camp Summer Fun Grades: 1-5

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: Camp Summer Fun is all about discovering new friendships, enjoying arts and crafts, playing lots of group games and participating in individual and team sports. On the first two Thursdays of the session, camp will travel to Centennial Beach and then on the last Thursday of the session, we'll take a field trip to a fun destination! On Thursdays, campers begin the day at 8:45 a.m. with pick up at 3:00 p.m. Campers need to bring a snack, drink and lunch each day. Camp will meet outdoors when weather permits. Fee includes Camp Summer Fun T-shirt to wear on field trip days. Detailed information about camp is located at www.napervilleparks.org/camps (dn)

name: Camp Toadstools & Pollywogs

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3y 6m but less than 6 yrs

description: From playing in the mud to climbing over logs, this camp is for adventurers who love to be in nature. Each week features new, nature-based crafts, games, activities and outdoor adventures. Please dress appropriately. Gym shoes are required, no flip-flops. Campers must be toilet-trained and be able to separate from caregiver. Please send a water bottle each day. If your child has allergies or asthma that require an Epi-pen or inhaler to accompany your child, please contact Sara Cass at scass@napervilleparks.org to complete the necessary paperwork at least 5 days before the start of camp. (sc)

name: Chess Wizards

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Join us this summer for tons of challenging chess lessons, exciting games and cool prizes. You'll improve your chess skills, meet new friends and work out your most powerful muscle - your brain! Our camps include fun team chess games (like bughouse), recess time, snacks, tournaments and puzzles. Each camper receives a T-shirt, trophy and puzzle folder. Unleash your brain power and spend part of your summer break with Chess Wizards! Our interactive curriculum makes learning fun for new and seasoned players alike. (bd)

name: Choreography For Fun!

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: Dancers will explore a variety of styles, including jazz, modern, hip-hop, lyrical, and more. Each session introduces fresh combinations that challenge technique, musicality, and expression, allowing students to expand their movement vocabulary while building confidence and versatility. The class emphasizes both precision and artistry, encouraging dancers to connect with the music and tell a story through movement. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: Code Ninjas-North

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Code Ninjas is a coding center designed specifically for kids in a unique dojo-inspired learning environment. This program emphasizes project-based learning, where students build real games and apps, ensuring that they gain practical hands-on experience with coding. Educational concepts taught in this program include basic programming principles, game development, app creation, logical thinking and problem solving, mathematics and computational thinking, teamwork and collaboration, user interface design, debugging and troubleshooting. Code Ninjas North is located at 2765 Maple Ave. in Lisle just east of Naper Blvd. (jg)

name: Code Ninjas-South

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Code Ninjas is a coding center designed specifically for kids in a unique dojo-inspired learning environment. This program emphasizes project-based learning, where students build real games and apps, ensuring that they gain practical hands-on experience with coding. Educational concepts taught in this program include basic programming principles, game development, app creation, logical thinking and problem solving, mathematics and computational thinking, teamwork and collaboration, user interface design, debugging and troubleshooting. Code Ninjas South is located at 3108 Route 59, Suite 144 in Naperville at the southeast corner of Route 59 and 95th St. (jg)

name: Deep Water Test Prep

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Classes are designed to help students pass the Centennial Beach deep water test. To pass the Centennial Beach deep water test students must be able to swim 100 meters of freestyle without stopping and with continuous proper form. Participants will build on their foundational knowledge of freestyle. Class size is generally a maximum of 5 students per instructor. The Centennial Beach Deep Water Swim test is offered at 12:50 pm, 2:50 pm and 5:50 pm daily in the lap lanes. Once the swimmer has successfully passed the test during the current season, they are issued a wristband at the Beach each time they visit. The wristband must be worn at all times during their visit so they are identified as a swimmer who can use the deep end. (cj)

name: Dementia-Friendly Movie Musicals

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Made for dementia participants and their family members/caregivers, enjoy movie musicals from the '20s to the '80s in the comfortably decorated lounge with movie theatre seats. Bring back fond memories while reminiscing about times that made you laugh and smile. The run time for each movie varies, but each shouldn't last more than two hours and fifteen minutes. Although this program is free, registration is required. This is a per person event; every dementia participant and family member/caregiver must register. (jg)

name: Digging Dinosaurs

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: Journey to the prehistoric land of dinosaurs. This camp incorporates arts, crafts, games and stories to teach pint-sized paleontologists about these amazing extinct creatures. Campers must be toilet-trained and be able to separate from parent/caregiver. Please, no flip-flops. If your child has allergies or asthma that require an Epi-pen or inhaler to accompany your child, please contact Sara Cass at scass@napervilleparks.org to complete the necessary paperwork at least 5 days before the start of camp. (sc)

name: Elements of Art Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 8 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Enjoy summer art fun and more artistic discoveries! Our staff will be glamming up participants with hair flower, make-up sparkle and pretty nail polish application complete with flower nail stickers. They will decorate a craft with paints, stencils and flower embellishments and jewels. They will also design a fun beaded bracelet with Hawaiian charms. Each participant will receive a take home outfit of a flower lei and a flowered Hawaiian skirt for photos at our palm tree backdrop and props. The class ends with maraca freeze dance and limbo line! name: Good Times Day Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 10 yrs

description: Good Times Day Camp is the perfect choice for families looking for the district's popular full day camp activities but want access to an indoor location throughout the day. This full-day, week-long camp keeps kids having fun all summer! They'll discover new friendships, enjoy arts and crafts, play group games and participate in individual and team sports. Camp will travel to Centennial Beach twice a week to swim and take a field trip to a fun destination once each week. Campers need to bring their lunch each day except Thursday when a pizza, chips and lemonade lunch is provided. Fee includes Good Times Day Camp T-shirt to wear on field trip days. Early pickup is available at 3:00 p.m. each day except Friday field trip days. Registration numbers for day camps are closed on the Wednesday of the week prior to camp. Registrations for day camps are accepted only up to a determined maximum number. Closing of registrations for day camp is being implemented in order for the Park District to monitor camp enrollment and ensure proper staffing levels. All detailed information about camp is located at www.napervilleparks.org/camps. (dn)

After demonstrating mastery in one level, the student skater may proceed to the next. The curriculum works in conjunction with USFS Basic Skills Program that is taught in quality rinks worldwide. description: Experienced Kids First Sports Safety, Inc. coaches teach different sports each day giving kids a chance to learn about new sports and play their favorites. General rules are introduced including safety and fundamentals before the game is played. Choices may include baseball/softball, soccer, flag football, T-ball/Blast ball, kickball, dodgeball and balloon ball. In case of rainout, time will be added to the remaining days of camp. (ba)

name: Kids First Multi-Sport Program

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 14 yrs

description: Experienced Kids First Sports Safety, Inc. coaches teach different sports each day giving kids a chance to learn about new sports and play their favorites. General rules are introduced including safety and fundamentals, and then the game is played. Choices may include baseball/softball, soccer, badminton, flag football, T-ball/Blast ball, kickball, dodgeball and water balloon toss. (ba)

name: Kids First Softball Fundamentals Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: This camp challenges both new and experienced players using competitive softball drills and games that maximize player potential. Players learn skills in pitching, fielding, running, batting and throwing. Proper body balance and first-step directional movements are emphasized. Parents are invited to the championship game on the final day of camp. Players should bring their glove and a water bottle. In case of rainout, time is added equally to remaining sessions. Taught by Kids First Sports Safety, Inc. staff. (ba)

name: Kids First Speed Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: Coaches focus on teaching sprints, hurdles, jumps, running and throws in a safe and fundamental way. The program consists of body-balance techniques and speed and quickness and agility drills designed to produce a safer, more powerful athlete. A series of team relay races makes the program fun and entertaining. In case of rainout, time is added equally to remaining sessions. Conducted by Kids First Sports Safety, Inc. (ba)

name: Kids First Track & Field Fundamentals Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: This program introduces young participants to the timed events that make up the sport of track and field. Coaches will teach sprints, hurdles, jumps, distance running and throws in a safe and fundamental way. Participants learn new techniques and strengthen existing skills. There will be a mini-meet on the final day. In case of rainout, time is added equally to remaining sessions. Conducted by coaches from Kids First Sports Safety, Inc. (ba)

name: Kids First Ultimate Frisbee® Fundamentals Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 16 yrs

description: Ultimate Frisbee is one of the fastest growing sports in the country today. It is a simple team sport that has been described as a combination of football, soccer and basketball. Certified coaches prepare players to play, enjoy and be successful. Learn basic rules, how to throw and score points offensively and how to protect the goal defensively. Parents are invited to the championship match at the end of the last day. In case of rainout, time is added equally to remaining sessions. Taught by Kids First Sports Safety, Inc. staff. (ba)

name: Kids First Volleyball Fundamentals

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 14 yrs

description: Get started playing the fun, action-packed game of volleyball. Learn fundamental techniques incorporating balance, directional movements, ball handling and sportsmanship through skills drills, visual volleyball safety instruction and games. Conducted by Kids First Sports Safety, Inc. staff. (ba)

name: Kids First Volleyball Fundamentals Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: This fun, action-packed camp prepares you for success playing volleyball. Players learn fundamental techniques incorporating balance, directional movements, ball handling and sportsmanship through skills drills, visual volleyball safety instruction and games. Conducted by Kids First Sports Safety, Inc. staff. (ba)

name: Kids' Night Out: End of Summer Extravaganza

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Enjoy the night out, while your children celebrate the end of summer with these fun activities: Popsicles, dance party, games and more. Dinner and juice is provided. Register online or at the Fort Hill Activity Center main service desk. Fitness members must register in person or over the phone to receive discount. (km)

name: Laugh Out Loud Improv

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 9 yrs but less than 14 yrs

description: If you enjoy comedy, laughing, acting, or just having a good time, this is one program you don't want to miss! Create characters, play awesome theater games, invent scenes, develop social skills and be spontaneous. No class July 3. (sl)

name: Leaps and Turns

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 19 yrs

description: Leaps and Turns consists of various drills and exercises used to improve technique. This class is dedicated to improving extension, turns, and leaps, working both the right and left sides equally. Younger students will focus on basic drills, while exercises will gradually increase in difficulty as students become more advanced. The goal of the class is to break down the steps learned in other classes and perfect them. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: LEGO: Pro Sports Lab Using LEGO® Materials

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 9 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Step into the world of sports engineering in this LEGO®-powered challenge! Students collaborate to design and build advanced stadiums, engineer machines that replicate real sports movements and develop innovative games. Throughout the camp, teams compete in fun, hands-on engineering challenges that test their creativity, problem-solving and design skills, all while building teamwork and engineering confidence one brick at a time. (jg)

name: LEGO: Sports Lab Using LEGO® Materials

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 9 yrs

description: Get ready to bring your favorite sports to life, from the basketball court to the sandy beach, in an action-packed LEGO® adventure! Design awesome stadiums, build cool machines that mimic real sports moves and create exciting games that can be played solo or with friends. Together, you will use your creativity and teamwork skills to engineer, build and compete, making every moment a blast! (jg)

name: Little Actors' Club

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: Shining Star Productions presents an innovative drama program that helps develop imagination and introduces little actors to the stage. Each week is an exciting new adventure with props, music, and games. Club members learn theater terms and gain enhanced spontaneity and self-esteem. (sl)

name: Little Scientist Camp Series

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: This camp is designed for budding scientists with the focus on the joy of discovery, the magic of why and the thrill of the "aha" moment. Campers will participate in hands-on experiments that tickle the imagination while fostering a foundational love for the wonders of the world. Join us for one week or multiple weeks. Campers must be toilet-trained and be able to separate from parent/caregiver. Please, no flip-flops. If your child has allergies or asthma that require an Epi-pen or inhaler to accompany your child, please contact Sara Cass at scass@napervilleparks.org to complete the necessary paperwork at least 5 days before the start of camp. (sc) Stem: Join us as we explore engineering by building towers, bridges, catapults, marble coasters and more! Ocean: Ever wonder how whales stay warm or why beaches erode or how light dictates what lives in the layers of the ocean? Join us as we explore the wonders of the ocean! Space: Suit up and blast into space! Learn about astronauts and explore the galaxy. Cooking: Edible science week where children can really eat their science experiments. Water & Ice: This week, we will be exploring the properties of water through fun, hands-on activities. Chemistry: This week is all about chemical reactions, osmosis, emulsification and more! Physics: This week, we will be exploring matter, surface tension, buoyancy and more! Insects: Buzz, crawl, and flutter into a week of insect discovery! Preschool campers will study butterflies, ants, bees, ladybugs, and more through sensory play, storytelling, science experiments, and creative art projects.

name: Martial Arts: ISKC Karate Adult

age_range.raw_age_text: 15 yrs +

description: Illinois Shotokan Karate Club is Chicagoland's premier karate school taught under the instruction of John DiPasquale, a four-time National Champion, US National Coach and President of the US National Karate Federation. The adult program releases tension, develops total body fitness and builds stamina and overall productivity! In addition to self-defense skills, karate increases flexibility, cardiovascular endurance and muscle tone while improving core strength. (fg) Uniforms and Belt-Testing are options available through the ISKC instructor. Youth, Parent/Child and Adult classes may train together. Beginner students are not permitted to register for the current session after the second class has met. Registration for continuers through advanced students is accepted after the start date, but payment of the full fee is required.

name: Martial Arts: ISKC Karate Parent/Child

age_range.raw_age_text: 7 yrs +

description: Illinois Shotokan Karate Club is Chicagoland's premier karate school taught under the instruction of John DiPasquale, a four-time National Champion, US National Coach and President of the US National Karate Federation. The parent/child program is a great way to spend quality time with your child while conditioning muscles, developing coordination and improving cardiovascular fitness. (fg) Uniforms and Belt-Testing are options available through the ISKC instructor. Youth, Parent/Child and Adult classes may train together. Beginner students are not permitted to register for the current session after the second class has met. Registration for continuers through advanced students is accepted after the start date, but payment of the full fee is required.

name: Martial Arts: ISKC Karate Youth

age_range.raw_age_text: 7 yrs +

description: Illinois Shotokan Karate Club is Chicagoland's premier karate school taught under the instruction of John DiPasquale, a four-time National Champion, US National Coach and President of the US National Karate Federation. ISKC?s youth program puts children in touch with their bodies and offers a good mix of strength training with cardiovascular and flexibility exercises. Children increase their coordination, agility and poise, as well as learn lasting personal safety skills. They also benefit from the mental stimulation of learning the choreographed moves of the kata and the discipline of conforming to class rules. (fg) Uniforms and Belt-Testing are options available through the ISKC instructor. Youth, Parent/Child and Adult classes may train together. Beginner students are not permitted to register for the current session after the second class has met. Registration for continuers through advanced students is accepted after the start date, but payment of the full fee is required.

name: Martial Arts: ISKC Karate/Pre-Karate and Safety

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 7 yrs

description: Illinois Shotokan Karate Club is Chicagoland's premier karate school taught under the instruction of John DiPasquale, a four-time National Champion, US National Coach and President of the US National Karate Federation.

name: Martial Arts: Kid's Karate Club and SafetyTime

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: This progressive martial arts program teaches the basics in karate, self-defense, sparring, kata and children's safety with belt progression through Black Belt. It is taught in a unique way where children are encouraged to have fun and gain confidence. The program targets many building blocks including respect, self-esteem, self-confidence and leadership, but most importantly, family involvement. Parents may participate with their children at no cost as part of the Parent Helper Program. There is a Mandatory Uniform Requirement required for this program, details will be give at first class. For more information, visit www.kidskarate.com. (fg)

name: Martial Arts: Kids Kung Fu

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: The focus in all levels is on building character and personal achievement and not in aggression and competition. Students earn increasingly higher belts as they progress in knowledge and abilities. Information regarding additional costs for T-shirts required for Level 2 & 3 will be discussed at first class and will be purchased directly through instructor. (bn) Level 1 - Students begin with simple exercises and routines that develop confidence and self-discipline as well as build coordination and strength. Level 2 - Students proceed through more difficult routines that demand a higher level of focus and concentration. Two-person Kung Fu practice is introduced that allows the students to develop their skills together. Instructor approval is required. Level 3 - This level is for those students that are on the road to their Kung Fu Black Belt. Training in child-appropriate staff and sword is introduced along with child-appropriate martial arts applications. Instructor approval is required.

name: Mean Girls

age_range.raw_age_text: 21 yrs +

description: Paramount Theatre, Aurora This hilarious musical has heart, telling the story of Cady Heron, a sweet and smart new girl who has just moved from Africa to suburban Illinois. When she enters the wild world of North Shore High, she quickly finds herself tangled up with The Plastics, the school's most popular and most ruthless clique led by queen bee Regina George. As Cady tries to fit in, she learns that popularity comes with a price, and revenge can get ugly fast. Seats are on the main floor. Lunch includes hot entree, potato or rice, vegetable, rolls, dessert and beverage. Price includes transportation, lunch and theatre ticket. (bn)

name: Meditation for Youth

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: This program is much more than just a basic class on calming the body and mind. Participants will learn the tools needed for managing a multitude of concerns including stress, anxiety, emotions, family togetherness, and more. As they progress from youth and adolescence, participants will benefit from understanding the importance of mindfulness and coping skills. Jitendra Desai employs the right method for teaching and helping students tap into the proper ways of handling difficult situations that arise. (km)

name: Mini Music Makers

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6m but less than 6 yrs

description: Make music with your little one! Join local music school, Edge Music Academy, for an early childhood music class led by a licensed, board-certified music therapist. This is a sing-along experience with percussion instruments and other fun accessories, perfect for young children to explore music in an intimate, hands-on setting. A parent or caregiver must be present for all class times due to the young age of students. (sl)

name: Modern/Contemporary: Adult Beginner

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Learn the fundamentals of modern/contemporary dance while strengthening and toning your body and increasing your flexibility. This program is perfect for students new to the modern/contemporary style of dance or those looking to return to the art. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: Music for Little Mozarts

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 8 yrs

description: This class is designed to give your child an exciting introduction to more formal piano instruction. Students will learn musical concepts as they relate to the keyboard while developing singing, movement, and listening skills simultaneously with an introduction to musical styles. The required lesson and workbooks are available from the instructor at the first class for $15. (sl)

name: Music Makers Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: Love to move and grove? This camp is for you! Sing, dance and make musical instruments. Campers must be toilet-trained and be able to separate from parent/caregiver. Please, no flip-flops. If your child has allergies or asthma that require an Epi-pen or inhaler to accompany your child, please contact Sara Cass at scass@napervilleparks.org to complete the necessary paperwork at least 5 days before the start of camp. (sc)

name: Musical Theater Dance: Junior

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 7 yrs

description: Do you dream of being on Broadway someday? In this class dancers will learn about the art of musical theater as they combine acting and dancing to create a spectacular performance. Each class focuses on dance technique, acting, and team building. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: Musical Theatre Featuring Disney Favorites!

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 8 yrs

description: The music of Disney provides a soundtrack to life! "Be Our Guest", "You've Got a Friend in Me", "Bibbity-Bobbity-Boo!", and "Let It Go!" just to name a few. Explore the Disney song list while collaborating to create an original script. Students will learn about the theatre, develop unique characters, and work together to create their original script. The session culminates in a one-of-a-kind performance. (sl)

name: Naperville Premier Soccer League University-1st Grade

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 8 yrs

description: The Naperville Premier Soccer League University is an opportunity for 1st grade teams to receive specialized training, while still cultivating a recreational experience. Teams receive one training session per week with a certified soccer trainer, and have games with their volunteer coach on Saturdays. This is a recreational program, no scores or standings are kept. Games are played against NYS teams and must follow the NYS policies such as no running-up of scores. Referees will not be utilized; teams will use parent volunteers and coaches as referees and linesmen. Players must wear the NYS reversible jersey. Non-residents are charged an additional $20 per player which is collected during the roster process. A $200 non-refundable deposit with auto-draw payment plan set-up or full payment is due at the time of registration. The last day to register or withdraw and receive a refund minus the $200 deposit is June 16. There are 7 games in the season and 9 weeks of training. Practices begin the week of August 25 and the first game is September 12. For additional information, please contact Susan Wasson at swasson@napervilleparks.org or www.napervilleparks.org/napervillepremiersoccerleague. (sa)

name: Naperville Premier Soccer League: 7/8th Boys

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 11 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: The Naperville Premier Soccer League is designed for teams seeking a program with an enhanced focused on player development and increased competition – still within a recreational environment. Optional technical and tactical training is provided weekly by a certified soccer trainer. Practice time and location is determined by the team and is based on trainer availability. There are 7 games in the season that take place on Saturdays at various parks in Naperville. Non-residents are charged an additional $20 per player which is collected during the roster process. The last day to register for a trainer option is June 16. The last day to register for the league-only option is June 30. A $200 non-refundable deposit with auto-draw payment plan set-up or full payment is due at the time of registration. Teams registering for a “trainer option” have until June 16 to withdraw and receive a refund, minus the $200 deposit. After June 16, the training portion of the fee is non-refundable. Teams registering for “league-only” option have until June 30 to withdraw and receive a refund, minus the $200 deposit. After June 30 all fees are non-refundable. Practices start the week of August 25 with the first game scheduled for September 12. Teams are required to review the complete league details at www.napervilleparks.org/napervillepremiersoccerleague prior to registering. (sa)

name: Naperville Youth NFL FLAG Football

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: The Naperville Park District has partnered with the National Football League to offer this flag football league where players learn the game of football in a safe setting. Program emphasizes positive coaching and provides an environment where every child has the opportunity to succeed. Teams typically practice two nights weekly prior to the start of the game schedule and one night weekly once games begin. Practices take place between the hours of 4:00-7:00 p.m. for approximately 60-75 minutes. Participants play a seven-game schedule on Friday nights or Sunday afternoons beginning September 11. All games are played in Naperville at Commissioners Park, Nike Sports Complex, Knoch Park or Prairie Park. Volunteer parent coaches are needed . Players are contacted by their coach with the time of their practice during the week before the first practice. Each player receives an NFL team reversible jersey and an official NFL FLAG belt. Players must provide their own mouthguard. (ba)

name: Naperville Youth Soccer: Boys 1st Grade

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 8y 3m

description: Naperville Youth Soccer is a recreational program that emphasizes fun and learning. Participants will be a part of a team, learn new skills, socialize, be active and have fun! Weekly practice locations are listed below. Teams will practice between the hours of 4:30 and 7:00 p.m. for approximately one hour. Players will be contacted by their coaches one week prior to the start of the season with practice time, game schedule and other important season information. Games are played on Saturdays at various parks throughout Naperville. Game schedules are posted approximately one week prior to the start of the season at https://www.quickscores.com/napervilleparks. The Pre-K and K programs are age based; grade level not applicable. Pre-K participants must be 4 years old as of 9/1/2026. Kindergarten participants must be 5-6 years 3 months old as of 9/1/2026 and not in 1st grade. All other participants must register for the grade they are in during the fall season. Please register or waitlist for one team only. Anyone registered on a team AND on a waitlist will be removed from the waitlist without notice. Adult volunteer coaches are required for each team. Coaching preference is selected at time of registration. Coaches are assigned by order of registration. Coaches that are selected will receive their coaching information and assignments by mid August. Pre-K - 1st grade teams use parent volunteers and coaches as game referees and linesmen. The first practice is the week of August 24. There are 7 games with the first game scheduled for September 12. Participants must wear a NYS reversible jersey which is purchased separately and available for sale at the Fort Hill Activity Center. For complete league information, including uniform requirements, please visit https://www.napervilleparks.org/napervilleyouthsoccer. (sa)

Extra craft materials are available for an extra fee . Please Note: Quantities are limited. An email confirmation will be sent when your kit is ready to pick up. Pick up your kit inside the nature center.

name: Nature: Creek Critters Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 9 yrs

description: Prepare to get wet while you investigate the creek, pond and river at Knoch Knolls Park. Spend time wading in the river, catching fish and searching for aquatic critters. Bring a healthy snack and water bottle each day. An extra set of clothes is recommended. (ah)

name: Nature: Prehistoric Pals Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 7 yrs

description: Travel back in time to the age of the dinosaurs and the last ice age. Learn about different dinosaurs and giant dragonflies, our state fossil, the Tully Monster, and ice age animals like the woolly mammoth and saber-toothed cats! Bring a water bottle and healthy snack each day and wear clothes that can get wet and dirty. (ah)

name: NPSL Fall 2026 Waivers

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: These are waiver codes only for those who have already completed a TEAM registration. Participants must have permission from the coach of the team to register. Those without permission will be withdrawn. There is a $20 fee for non-residents. University (1st Grade): All players must be in 1st grade in order to be roster eligible. Players who are in an older grade may not participate on the team even if their age fits within the parameters set in the system for registration purposes. 2nd Grade: All players must be in 2nd grade in order to be roster eligible. Players who are in an older grade may not participate on the team even if their age fits within the parameters set in the system for registration purposes. 3rd-8th Grade: All players must be in the grade or a grade below which the team has registered for in order to be roster eligible. Players who are in an older grade may not participate on the team even if their age fits within the parameters set in the system for registration purposes.

name: NYS Academy: Threes

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 4 yrs

description: The NYS Academy program is a great opportunity for younger children to become part of our Naperville Youth Soccer tradition. This coed, practice-only program introduces basic soccer skills in a fun, active and social environment. Teams meet once a week for approximately 30 - 45 minutes. Weekly practice locations and times are listed below. Please register according to your player’s age as of 9/1/2026. Please register or waitlist for one team only. Anyone registered on a team AND on a waitlist will be removed from the waitlist without notice. Adult volunteer coaches are required for each team. Coaching preference is selected at time of registration. Coaches will be contacted and provided with age-appropriate lesson plans by August 14. Players will be contacted by their coach the week of August 16. For more information, please visit https://napervilleparks.org/napervilleyouthsocceracademy. (sa)
