name: NYS Pre-Season Coach Clinic

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 18 yrs but less than 99 yrs

description: Coaches interested in learning drills and skills to bring back to their teams are invited to attend a free hands-on coach clinic. Pre-registration is required.

name: Outdoor: Beach Yoga

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: Enjoy a relaxing and energizing yoga practice complete with the beautiful views of Centennial Beach. Bring a yoga mat and a beach towel and find joy as you spend time in the sand and grass overlooking the water. Leave feeling refreshed, focused, peaceful, grateful and strong. No previous yoga experience is required, only an open and positive attitude. (km)

name: Paddleboard Yoga

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: Enjoy practicing your favorite yoga routines on the water! Strengthen your core while developing better balance and coordination. Each class culminates in relaxation leaving you feeling refreshed, focused, peaceful, grateful and strong. You must be comfortable in and around the water. Minimal yoga experience is helpful, but not required. Arrive dressed to enter the water. Led by encouraging and experienced yoga instructor, Ann Gasperec. (km)

name: Paddlewheel Riverboat & Durant-Peterson House

age_range.raw_age_text: 21 yrs +

description: St. Charles, IL Start with a 1.5-hour private charter paddlewheel boat ride down a quiet and peaceful section of the Fox River. Learn about the history of the St. Charles area. Lunch on board will be served on the lower deck. Bagged lunch choices are a ham sub sandwich or turkey sub sandwich with chips, cookies and a drink. If you have dietary restrictions, please choose the applicable option during registration. Although there are nice views from the lower level and bow, head to the upper deck after lunch (12-15 steps) for a more expansive view. Visit the 1843 Durant-Peterson House museum. Docents dressed in period clothing will bring the group back in time to experience what life was like living on the Illinois Prairie in the late 1800s. Partake in an heirloom apple sampling. Learn the history of apples around the world and how apples became a vital part of pioneer life. There will be a variety of heirloom apples to taste and compare. Price includes transportation, lunch, boat ride, museum entrance with guide and apple tasting. (bn)

name: Parking Permits

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 15 yrs but less than 20 yrs

description: The Naperville Park District offers parking spaces for Neuqua Valley and Naperville Central High School students. Permit holders will be eligible for parking in the designated spaces at the Skate Park lot at Frontier, the gravel lot off of West Street or the designated spaces at the Centennial Beach parking lot. Permits purchased online will be mailed to the address listed on your account within two weeks of purchase. If you purchase online, your receipt will act as your confirmation of purchase until your receive your permit. Please print your receipt and place it on your dashboard until your permit arrives. Permits also may be purchased in person at the Alfred Rubin Riverwalk Community Center, the Knoch Knolls Nature Center or the Fort Hill Activity Center. Applications must be signed by a parent or guardian. Spaces are not assigned and are available first come, first served ONLINE REGISTRATION OPENS JULY 11, 2026. WALK IN WILL BE AVAILABLE JULY 11, 2026. CHECK WEBSITE FOR FACILITY HOURS. If you are participating in your school lottery for a permit, please wait for those results before purchasing an NPD parking permit.

name: Pickleball Adult Classes

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Pickleball is a fast-growing racket sport that is best described as a mix of badminton, tennis and ping-pong that can be played by nearly everyone. Program consists of instruction followed by actual game play. Players should wear athletic shoes and dress as for tennis. Equipment is provided, but bring your own Pickleball paddle if you have one. (ba)

name: Pickleball: Practice with the Pro Private Instruction

age_range.raw_age_text: 4 yrs +

description: Our pickleball pros are available for private or semi-private lessons scheduled at a mutually-convenient time. Two levels of lessons are available and may be scheduled with one to three persons in a group. Instruction with one of our teaching pros is available at a cost of $69 per hour. Lessons with one of our Certified Pros are $79 per hour. Purchase a five-lesson package and save. To schedule a private lesson, register for the lesson and a staff member will be in touch with you to schedule the day and time. Lesson cancelations must be done 24 hours in advance in order to receive a credit. (ba)

name: Pickleball: Practice with the Pro Private Instruction

age_range.raw_age_text: 4 yrs +

description: Our pickleball pros are available for private or semi-private lessons scheduled at a mutually-convenient time. name: Pirouette with Me

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 1y 6m but less than 4 yrs

description: Explore ballet with your little one in this special program that includes props, stories, music and more! It focuses on engaging little ones with familiar music in a high-energy environment introducing ballet technique while building coordination skills, memory and listening skills. Ballet shoes are optional for parent/caregiver. Adult is free and must accompany child; maximum two children per adult. Please register each child separately. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: Pottery

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: The unique environment of a pottery studio is relaxing and conducive to creativity. Learn basic hand-building and surfacing techniques, the production stages of glazing and how to design and develop projects. All supplies are included. (bd)

name: Pottery I

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 10 yrs

description: Build castles, make coil pots or create a favorite animal - the possibilities are endless! Learn basic hand-building techniques and the stages of the glazing process. Program may be repeated. All materials provided. Please wear old clothes. Parents please stop by Studio One the week after the session ends to pick up your child's items that they have created. (bd)

name: Pottery II

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 9 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Build on the basic techniques of this art and learn more advanced hand-building techniques. Both beginning and returning students are welcome. Please wear old clothes. All materials are provided. Parents please stop by Studio One the week after the session ends to pick up your child's items that they have created. (bd)

name: Pottery: Family Open Studio

age_range.raw_age_text: 3 yrs +

description: Join as a family, utilize the studio and receive guided pottery instruction. All materials provided. Come to class with ideas or photos of what you would like to make. Participants should wear old clothes or bring their own apron. Please register each person in the family. Multiple families may register for the same date until class size has reached a maximum of eight participants. (bd)

name: Pottery: Teen

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 12 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: Learn hand-building and surfacing techniques, the stages of the glazing process and how to design and develop projects. Please wear old clothes. All materials are provided. Parents please stop into Studio One at the beginning of the first class to confirm contact information, class times and participant pick up instructions. No class July 1 & 8. (bd)

name: Premier: Boxing/TRX

age_range.raw_age_text: 15 yrs +

description: Build posture, strength, balance, and mobility by leveraging body weight using TRX straps combined with the cardio power of boxing. Form and technique are instructor-monitored with any necessary modifications provided by certified boxing and TRX trainer(s) to enable participants to be safely challenged. Enjoy all the fun and challenge of a typical TRX class combined with elements of boxing. Participants need to bring their own boxing gloves. (km)

name: Premier: TRX

age_range.raw_age_text: 15 yrs +

description: Build posture, strength, flexibility, balance and mobility with the method of leveraging body weight. Every exercise is powered by the abdominals. Form technique is monitored and modifications provided by certified TRX trainers to enable you to be safely challenged. This program, which is for all levels, will challenge muscles to develop strength, stability and coordination. Fort Hill Fitness members: contact the Fort Hill Activity Center at 630-995-8900 to register. (km)

name: Premier: TRX 45

age_range.raw_age_text: 15 yrs +

description: All the fun and challenge of a typical TRX class in a 45-minute format! Build posture, strength, flexibility, balance and mobility with the method of leveraging body weight. Every exercise is powered by the abdominals. Form technique is monitored and modifications provided by certified TRX trainers to enable you to be safely challenged. This program, which is for all levels, will challenge muscles to develop strength, stability and coordination. Fort Hill Fitness members: contact the Fort Hill Activity Center at 630-995-8900 to register. (km)

name: Premier: TRX Gold

age_range.raw_age_text: 15 yrs +

description: Build posture, strength, flexibility, balance and mobility with the method of leveraging body weight. Every exercise is powered by the abdominals. Form technique is monitored and modifications provided by certified TRX trainers to enable you to be safely challenged. All the fun of a typical TRX class without having to get down on the floor! All the movements are with your feet planted firmly on the ground. Beginners and those looking for low impact, this class is for you! Fort Hill Fitness members: contact the Fort Hill Activity Center at 630-995-8900 to register. (km)

name: Premier: TRX Gold - Beginner

age_range.raw_age_text: 15 yrs +

description: This class is for the AOA (Active Older Adult) who is just starting out with TRX to learn the foundational movements. You will learn to build posture, strength, flexibility, balance and mobility with the method of leveraging body weight. Every exercise is powered by the abdominals. Form technique is monitored and modifications provided by certified TRX trainers to enable you to be safely challenged. All the fun of a typical TRX class without having to get down on the floor! All the movements are with your feet planted firmly on the ground. Beginners and those looking for low impact, this class is for you! Fort Hill Fitness members: contact the Fort Hill Activity Center at 630-995-8900 to register. (km)

name: Premier: TRX/GRIT

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: This TRX/GRIT class is designed to build strength, stability, and endurance. Using the TRX suspension trainer, participants engage in controlled, bodyweight movements that enhance full‑body strength, balance, core stability, and mobility. GRIT incorporates high‑intensity interval exercises to elevate heart rate, improve muscular endurance, and boost overall athletic performance. This dynamic, results‑driven workout is suitable for all fitness levels, with modifications and progressive options to meet each participant where they are. Expect to be challenged safely and confidently as you work toward your personal fitness goals. Fort Hill Fitness members, contact the Fort Hill Activity Center at 630-995-8900 to register. (km)

name: Private Voice Lessons

age_range.raw_age_text: 5 yrs +

description: Develop your voice and learn performance skills! Lessons include breathing, technical exercises and warm-ups. Our expert instructors will help pick perfect songs for your voice and style. You will be contacted by The Music Suite to schedule your lessons. Classes are 30 minutes long and there are 7 classes in a session. (sl)

name: Regain Your Balance

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Taught by instructor Cecilia Floyd-Carruthers, Regain Your Balance is specifically designed for seniors who are currently mobile and able to support themselves without assistance. As seniors progress and notice a decline in cognitive function, the biggest fear is falling. Consisting of three 15-minute segments of sitting, standing and walking, this class will help you build your confidence and regain or maintain your balance. Fall prevention and how to correctly fall to avoid injuries will be discussed. Please bring water for hydration and wear gym shoes with good support. In order to participate in the Regain Your Balance class, you must be mobile and able to support yourself without assistance. (bn)

name: Rhythm Express: Music and Babies

age_range.raw_age_text: Age less than 1y 6m

description: Your musical playgroup awaits! Recent studies have shown that music affects the physical, emotional and intellectual development of babies and children and strengthens cognitive and sensory development. Join other like-minded parents of babies and new walkers as we experience the positive effects of music. Register child only; parents attend for free. A sibling discount is available for this program. The discount will be applied at the time of registration. There will be a make-up class available on August 8 to students who miss a class during the session. (sl)

name: Rhythm Express: Ocean Creatures

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 1y 6m but less than 6 yrs

description: Experience a musical adventure featuring your favorite creatures in the ocean! Learn music concepts like fast and slow and high and low by singing, dancing, listening and playing simple rhythmic instruments. Register child only; parents attend for free. A sibling discount is available for this program. The discount will be applied at the time of registration. Children under 9 months old accompanying siblings are free. (sl)

name: Rhythm Express: Transportation GO GO GO!

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 1y 6m but less than 6 yrs

description: Explore all the ways we GO GO GO through music and movement. A high energy class for all your little ones who like to GO! Register child only; parents attend for free. A sibling discount is available for this program. The discount will be applied at the time of registration. Children under 17 months old accompanying an older sibling are free. There will be a make-up class available on August 8 to students who miss a class during the session. No class July 3. (sl)

name: RoboThink: Battle Transportation Bots Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: Explore the world of transportation with RoboThink as we build Trains, Planes & Automobile robots based on our favorite vehicles from the RoboThink curriculum! In this exciting robotics camp, students will use motors, gears, and mainboards and learn important engineering and robotics concepts as they bring their creations to life and take their STEM skills to new heights. Class often culminates in a friendly, exciting battle, so sign up now for a fun, high-energy week together! (bd)

name: RoboThink: Engineer Race Cars Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: Rev up your engines and hit the racetrack with RoboThink! Get ready for an adrenaline-pumping program where your student will build and race a fleet of extraordinary race cars. But that's not all! You’ll also dive deep into the fascinating world of automotive engineering, learning about transmissions, pistons, and differentials. Put on your racing gloves and join us for an epic ride! (bd)

name: RoboThink: Intro to Coding Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 8 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: Dive into the world of coding with RoboThink's Introduction to Coding program! Equipped with RoboThink's special software, your student will discover the fundamental concepts of coding in an engaging and enjoyable environment. From loops and conditions to variables, they'll gain a solid foundation in coding principles. Prepare to build exciting programs, no prior coding experience required, but basic computer skills and reading fluency are necessary. (bd)

name: RoboThink: Rumble Robotics Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 8 yrs

description: Welcome to Rumble Robotics, where the battleground is set, and the excitement is unmatched! In this high-energy program, students of all skill levels immerse themselves in thrilling battles, whether it's spinning tops, wind-up knights, or their very own handcrafted battle robots. The adrenaline-pumping action unfolds over an hour, offering a perfect blend of strategy, creativity, and friendly competition. No prior experience is required. Just bring your enthusiasm and get ready to rumble in a whirlwind of fun and laughter! (bd)

name: RoboThink: STEAM Art & Robotics Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: Think robotics is just about building bots? Think again! RoboThink’s STEAM Lab is where art and engineering collide in the most creative way. In this hands-on program, kids build a variety of machines from spirographs to kinetic sculptures that produce real art. Along the way, they explore famous artists and movements like Piet Mondrian’s geometry, Seurat’s pointillism, and Banksy’s street art. Students will also gain foundational knowledge in robotics and engineering concepts like gear ratios, DC motors, and mechanical design all while getting hands-on and having fun. It’s a perfect blend of education, creativity, and unforgettable experiences! Bring a smock and let’s get ready to have fun! (bd)

name: Semi-Private Ballet: Level 4/5 + Pointe

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 9 yrs but less than 19 yrs

description: Designed to prepare dancers for the study of pointe work, this program emphasizes strengthening exercises for the legs and feet. Pre-Pointe also may be recommended for a dancer who is physically unable to undertake the rigors of pointe work, but can benefit from the exercises offered. Dancers must also be 9 years of age and enrolled in Ballet: Level 2 or higher. Dancers will remain in Pre-Pointe until they are formally advanced by the instructor to study on pointe. Dancers may wear ballet shoes or pre-pointe shoes. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: Semi-Private Beginner Piano

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: Experience a hands-on introduction to piano with instructors from Edge Music Academy! In this interactive, personalized semi-private lesson, get a taste for what it's like to learn to play the piano. EMA's lesson philosophy focuses on providing a strong foundation of music fundamentals and technique, while allowing students to explore playing in a wide variety of styles that appeal to your child's interests. The fee includes a required piano book. (sl)

name: Seminar: How Taxes Impact Retirement Income

age_range.raw_age_text: 40 yrs +

description: If you are nearing retirement or already retired, you need to understand how taxes impact your retirement income, as it may be possible to pay less in taxes on your hard-earned dollars. Learn the most up-to-date and comprehensive information regarding retirement taxation, including ways to efficiently harvest income sources, whether they are Social Security, 401K/IRA, other sources or a combination of them all. Presentation provided by Greg Kurinec. Although this program is free, registration is required. (bn)

name: Senior Kung Fu

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Senior Kung Fu is for the active senior looking for a different type of exercise. Come and have fun learning something new! The class consists of exercises, stance training, Kung Fu Forms (routines of movements), staff routines and two-person applications. (bn)

name: Senior Stretch

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Most exercise classes include stretching during warmup and cool down, but what about an entire class dedicated to this important activity? Stretching is vital for seniors and allows for greater movement in joints while improving overall posture in addition to releasing muscle tension and soreness, reducing the risk of injury. It also may help increase circulation, muscle control and improve balance and coordination. This 30-minute class, taught by Cecilia Floyd-Carruthers, covers stretching exercises from head to toe in a seated position as well as standing, using a chair for balance. Please bring water for hydration and wear gym shoes with good support. In order to participate in the Senior Stretch class, you must be mobile and able to support yourself without assistance. (bn)

name: Sewing Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 19 yrs

description: Join us for an introductory sewing class! Participants will learn how to thread a machine, wind a bobbin, and sew straight lines. Sewing machines will be provided for use in class. If you have your own working sewing machine, you are welcome to bring it. All supplies needed will be provided by the instructor. Supply fee is $25 payable to instructor at first class. (bd)

name: Sewing Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 19 yrs

description: Join us for an introductory sewing class! Participants will learn how to thread a machine, wind a bobbin, and sew straight lines. Sewing machines will be provided for use in class. If you have your own working sewing machine, you are welcome to bring it. All supplies needed will be provided by the instructor. Supply fee is $25 payable to instructor at first class. (bd)

name: Shape and Tone

age_range.raw_age_text: 15 yrs +

description: Reshape and tone your body through the use of weights, squats, Pilates moves, push-ups and much more! This program increases bone density through the use of muscle-strengthening exercises and is suitable for all levels. (km)

name: SHIP-August

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: SHIP is the Illinois State Health Insurance Assistance Program. Whether you are new to Medicare or already enrolled, SHIP is a great way to get information and answers about health insurance coverage for seniors. If you are considering a prescription drug plan, please bring your Medicare card, any other insurance cards and a list of your medications, including dosage and frequency to your appointment. If you would like to see if you might be eligible for financial help in paying for Medicare, bring your most recent tax return. Open Enrollment occurs every year between October 15 and December 7. Appointments during this time frame are for those who would like to review their Medicare Part C coverage or Part D prescription plans to insure you have the most comprehensive, cost efficient coverage for the upcoming year. Information on health insurance coverage for seniors includes the following: Medicare A & B (hospital/doctor), Medicare C (Medicare Advantage Plans/HMO, PPO, PFFS), Medicare D (Prescription Drug Plans), Medicare Supplemental Policies (Medigap), Long Term Care Insurance and Medicaid Programs. Counselors are trained and sponsored by the State of Illinois Department on Aging. Appointments are available between 9:00 a.m. and 12:00 p.m. To register, call 630-848-5000 or go online to napervilleparks.org to book an appointment with a SHIP counselor. (jg)

name: Small Group Piano

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 11 yrs

description: Group piano classes are a fantastic way for students to learn music in a fun and supportive environment. Our group piano lessons provide students with the opportunity to learn from experienced and knowledgeable teachers, and to practice alongside their peers. By learning together in a group setting, students develop important social skills like teamwork, cooperation, and communication. Each student has access to their own digital piano during the lesson. A required lesson book is available at the first class for $18. (sl)

name: Soccer League: Adult

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: The Naperville Park District Adult Soccer League is designed for teams looking for a fun, recreational experience. Men and women are welcome to participate. Play takes place on a reduced-size field with eight players per side. Teams play a seven game schedule. There is a $20/person non-resident fee in addition to the team fee. The league coordinator will be in touch with captains prior to the start of the season with additional information. Last day to register (pending availability) or withdraw and receive a refund is August 23. (sa)

name: Soccer: 5 Star Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 14 yrs

description: The 5 Star Soccer Camps are proud to offer a fresh, enthusiastic approach to teaching youth soccer. We pride ourselves in delivering a curriculum that presents the most current and advanced information on the development of the youth soccer player. The quality of our staff is among the best around, working hard to build on fundamental technique, while creating an atmosphere that unlocks the game within each child. We believe in our program, designed for success, that presents a positive, enjoyable environment for learning from energetic coaches in youth soccer. Program of instruction designed by Michael Wiggins, 2 time Illinois High School Soccer Coach of the Year and Head Coach of the 2014 Illinois HS State Champions. (sa)

name: Soccer: Chicago Fire FC Development Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 14 yrs

description: Chicago Fire FC Camps are the perfect way to introduce your child to the world's fastest-growing youth sport and develop their soccer skills. Through small group instruction, certified, professional coaches will guide campers through activities structured around daily themes, including dribbling, passing, attacking, and defending. Chicago Fire FC Camps incorporate nationally recognized SEL (Social and Emotional Learning) traits and values like self-awareness, responsible decision-making, and teamwork into activities. All participants receive a Chicago Fire camp t-shirt, and a ticket to a Chicago Fire match. Along with the ticket comes a special matchday experience including player autographs, an appearance by the lovable Fire mascot, Sparky, and discounted tickets for the whole family. (sa)

name: Social Bridge Lessons for Beginners

age_range.raw_age_text: 40 yrs +

description: Bridge is a fun and intellectually stimulating game that can be enjoyed for a lifetime. This is a friendly and relaxed six-week course designed for beginners. It will introduce you to the fundamentals of social bridge, including basic bidding and responding, play of the cards, and special situations. Each session combines instruction with guided practice, so you can learn by playing. Whether you are looking to meet new people, challenge your mind, or learn a new hobby, this course is the perfect place to start. No previous experience is necessary. While the course is free, registration and regular attendance are required. (bn)

name: Softball:  Coed 50+ Senior League

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Men and women age 50 and over gather on Monday, Wednesday and Friday mornings for informal pick-up game of 12" slow-pitch softball and socialization. Bring your glove and a desire to have fun. Registration is required, but teams are changed every week; come when you can! Program will not meet on Memorial Day or Labor Day. Play starts at 10:00 a.m. during the month of May due to cooler mornings. Questions may be directed to Rich Fleming at rflem9308@gmail.com. Fee includes a T-shirt. (ba)

name: Softball: Adult Team Registration

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Do you love to play softball? Many slow pitch softball leagues for men's and coed teams are offered. League play begins in early May. Top teams in each division participate in league playoffs. Captains of returning teams are notified by e-mail of organizational meetings and registration deadlines. All team fees as listed plus $20 per nonresident player. CoRec league uses the 14" "Mushball" and special CoRec rules. (ba)

name: Softball: Individual Registration

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Want to play, but don't have a team? This season, we plan to form one team from individual registrants to play in the 12" recreational division, one team in the Men's 12" 40+ Masters division, and one team in the CoRec 14" Wednesday division. You must be 18 or older by May 4. We'll e-mail schedules to all players in late April. Fee includes a jersey. A volunteer captain is needed for this team. name: Springboard Diving

age_range.raw_age_text: 8 yrs +

description: By training on both the three-meter and one-meter boards, divers learn the fundamentals of springboard diving. Beginning and intermediate divers are welcome. Divers must be able to swim 50 meters of freestyle in deep water. Class size is generally a maximum of 5 students per instructor. Make up classes, only due to facility closures, will be conducted on the Thursday and Friday of the 2nd week of the session. (cj)

name: Storybook Dance

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

Using costumes, lively music and storytelling, fairy tales become real and each beloved character comes to life. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: Stretch and Strengthen

Benefits of this class includes increased range of motion, greater flexibility, decreased risk of injury and reduced muscle soreness. Psychological benefits include an increased sense of well-being, confidence, greater body awareness and improved concentration. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: Summer Neon Dance Glam Night

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 11 yrs

Participants will decorate a neon drawstring summer bag as well as design a fun beaded anklet with a summer charm. Class ends with dancing to neon lights and fun pop music. A cool neon backdrop and summer props will be in room for some great pics. Each participant will leave with a summer themed glam bag of goodies! This is a drop-off independent class; parents do not stay. (bd)

name: Swim Lessons: Beach Adult

age_range.raw_age_text: 15 yrs +

description: Adult swim instruction is designed to improve skills and comfort in the water. All adults ages 15 and up who want to learn and improve their swimming skills are encouraged to register. name: Swim Lessons: Beach Level 1

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: This program is designed to improve each child's swimming skills at his or her own pace. Among other skills, students learn to put their faces in the water, float and flutter kick. More importantly, they learn to trust their instructors and realize that swimming is fun! Class size is generally a maximum of 4 students per instructor. Make up classes, only due to facility closures, will be conducted on the Thursday and Friday of the 2nd week of the session. (bs)

name: Swim Lessons: Beach Level 2

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs

Swimmers are placed by skill level and each participant learns water safety skills appropriate to their level. Level 2 builds upon the skills learned in Level 1. Students learn to add arms to their flutter kick to create a solid foundation in freestyle and backstroke. Class size is generally a maximum of 4 students per instructor. Make up classes, only due to facility closures, will be conducted on the Thursday and Friday of the 2nd week of the session. (cj)

name: Swim Lessons: Beach Level 3

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs

Swimmers are placed by skill level and each participant learns water safety skills appropriate to their level. Level 3 is taught in the deeper water. This level aims to equip students with water safety and survival skills. Students learn backstroke, jump in and recover to the surface, and explore swimming in deeper water guided by the instructor. Class size is generally a maximum of 4 students per instructor. Make up classes, only due to facility closures, will be conducted on the Thursday and Friday of the 2nd week of the session. (cj)

name: Swim Lessons: Beach Level 4

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: This program is designed to improve each child's swimming skills at his or her own pace. Swimmers are placed by skill level and each participant learns water safety skills appropriate to their level. Level 4 students work to refine their freestyle and backstroke, are introduced to treading water, work on shoulder rotation, and add an eight-beat kick, and bilateral breathing. age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: This program is designed to improve each child's swimming skills at his or her own pace. Level 5 students learn sidestroke and elementary backstroke as a building block to learning butterfly and breaststroke. Class size is generally a maximum 5 students per instructor. Make up classes, only due to facility closures, will be conducted on the Thursday and Friday of the 2nd week of the session. (cj)

name: Swim Lessons: Private Lessons

age_range.raw_age_text: 3 yrs +

description: Private swim lessons are taught one-on-one and tailored to meet the needs of each individual swimmer. Make up classes, only due to facility closures, will be conducted on Fridays. (cj)

name: Tai Chi: Adult & Senior-Practice and Instructional

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Looking for better balance, gentle movement, stress relief and moving meditation? Tai Chi might be just what you are looking for and it will complement your other exercise routines. The many benefits of Tai Chi including maintaining mobility, agility, health and vitality can be found in these simple movements. See why Tai Chi has been practiced for centuries to benefit the mind and body. Practice vs Instructional Classes: Practice classes have minimal instruction allowing the student to just follow along in the various exercises and movements to focus on relaxing and breathing. Every level Practice class has a corresponding level Instructional class. Instructional classes provide detailed explanation of everything contained in the Practice class. Ideally, a student would take both. Adult vs Senior Classes: Adult and Senior Tai Chi classes have the same content and instruction. Senior classes are priced for those 50 and over. Anyone 60 and over can register for an Adult Tai Chi class and receive a 20% senior discount. In Person vs Virtual vs Hybrid: Some classes are in person only; some are virtual only (via Zoom) and some are hybrid. Hybrid classes are simultaneously offered in person and via Zoom. If you cannot attend an in-person class on a specific date, you can participate at home via Zoom. (jg)

name: Tai Chi: Adult Advanced Two Person Energy Work

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Adult Advanced Two Person Energy Work is for the advanced student and participation in this class requires the permission of Master Troy. This class is for students already taking Advanced Tai Chi classes and are interested in developing their Tai Chi energy by working with other students and learning an advanced Tai Chi Form. Classes meet on designated Saturdays. The add-on option is for students also registered for two other classes with Master Troy. All others use the stand-alone option. (bn)

name: Tap/Jazz Basics

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: This program is designed to build a solid dance foundation. Dancers learn proper posture and technique while being introduced to dance terminology from both dance styles. The program focuses on the fundamentals of jazz technique, while incorporating tap to help with rhythm, tempo and distribution of weight. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: Tap: Adult Beginning

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: This tap program presents the rhythms and sounds of tap dance in a fun and upbeat way. As dancers progress, they add on to beginning rhythms and steps while sharpening their memory and improving coordination. Program explores more complex techniques and patterns while challenging the students to open their tap dance movement vocabulary, increasing their confidence and tap dance knowledge. This program is perfect for students new to tap, those looking to return to dance, or wanting to try something new. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: Tennis: A Taste of Tennis

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 11 yrs

description: This camp is designed for kids who want a great introduction to tennis. Instruction follows the USTA's 10-and-under pathway which utilizes smaller courts, special balls and smaller racquets. Camp emphasizes the ABCs - agility, balance and coordination. Please wear tennis shoes. In case of rainout, makeup will be on Friday. (ba)

name: Tennis: Adult Competitive Clinic

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Intermediate Level (NTRP Rating 2.7-3.4) and Advanced level players (NTRP ranking 3.5+) benefit from this clinic that focuses on singles and doubles strategies, shot consistency, specialty shots, difficult shots and serves. Players enrolled at the incorrect level may be removed. In case of rain, one makeup will be held. (ba)

name: Tennis: Adult Drill & Play

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: This class is designed for adults who have progressed beyond the beginner level and are able to rally consistently. Players should be comfortable with the basic strokes and ready to refine their technique while continuing to build confidence and consistency during live play. Instruction will focus on improving stroke mechanics, court positioning, and shot selection. This 90-minute class emphasizes skill development through dynamic drills, point play, and match based situations. Participants will also work on scoring, strategy, and structured match play to support continued growth and on-court decision making. Participants must bring their own racket, water, and gym shoes. One makeup class will be offered in the event of inclement weather. This class is not intended for beginner-level players. (ba)

name: Tennis: Adult Outdoor

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: This class is designed for adults who are new to tennis or who have taken one or two beginner classes. Participants will learn the fundamental tennis strokes, including forehands, backhands, volleys, and serves, while developing overall consistency and confidence on the court. Instruction will also cover scoring, rules, and basic match play so players feel comfortable playing points and games. This 90-minute class focuses on development drills and repetition, emphasizing the basics of tennis in a supportive learning environment. Participants must bring their own racquet, water, and gym shoes. One makeup class will be offered in the event of inclement weather. This class is strictly for beginner-level players. (ba)

name: Tennis: Cardio Tennis

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Coaches blast music and fast, tough feeds to get your heart pumping. The NTRP rating of 2.5-3.4 is adhered to as drills are designed for players who already have a foundation of skills and the athleticism to really hustle. Players who are not at an appropriate level are offered alternative program options. Please bring water and a towel. If class is canceled due to weather, one makeup will be held at the end of the session.(ba)

name: Tennis: Junior

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: Learn to play or improve your tennis game with the Park District's experienced staff. Students should dress in comfortable clothing, wear tennis shoes and provide their own racquet. Players are grouped by ability. Classes utilize the ABCs - agility, balance and coordination - along with instruction on basic tennis strokes. Orange Ball class will use a 60' tennis court and special orange tennis balls. Green Ball classes will use the Green Ball on a regular court. Yellow Ball classes use a standard tennis ball on a regular court. Beginners have never played tennis or have played a limited amount, but not on a regular basis. Class emphasizes introduction of forehand, backhand, serve, shot placement, positioning, scoring and rules. Advanced Beginners have knowledge of scoring and rules and may have had some lessons, but lack on-court experience. They can keep a ball in play with others of similar ability. Class emphasizes improvement of basic strokes and works on positioning, shot placement, footwork and serve consistency. Intermediates are those who can place shots with moderate success and sustain a rally at a slow pace. They are not yet comfortable with all strokes and lack consistency in serving. In case of rain, up to two makeups will be held at the completion of the session. (ba)

name: Tennis: Little Aces

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 8 yrs

description: Introduce your kids to a lifetime of tennis fun. We focus on the ABCs - agility, balance and coordination - using a variety of games, contests and other fun activities. Children learn basic tennis skills utilizing the USTA's 10-and-under tennis pathway on smaller courts using special racquets and red tennis balls. Children must wear tennis shoes; racquets are provided. In case of rain, one make up will be held at the end of the session.. (ba)

name: Tennis: Practice with the Pro Private Instruction

age_range.raw_age_text: 4 yrs +

description: Our tennis pros are available for private or semi-private lessons scheduled at a mutually-convenient time. Two levels of lessons are available and may be scheduled with one to three persons in a group. Instruction with one of our teaching pros is available at a cost of $69 per hour. Lessons with one of our USPTA/USPTR Certified Pros are $79 per hour. Purchase a five-lesson package and save 10%. Purchase a ten-lesson package and save 15%. To schedule a private lesson, register for the lesson and a staff member will be in touch with you to schedule the day and time. (ba)

name: Tennis: Rally Partner

age_range.raw_age_text: 4 yrs +

description: Improve your hitting consistency when you rally with one of our high school/college staff. Session does not include instruction, just plenty of fun hitting many, many tennis balls for a solid hour. Purchase a five-lesson package and save 10%. Register for the program and a staff member will be in touch with you to schedule the day and time. (ba)

name: The Buddy Holly Story

age_range.raw_age_text: 21 yrs +

description: Drury Lane Theatre, Oakbrook Terrace Discover the life and music of rock and roll pioneer Buddy Holly from his early start in Texas to his meteoric rise to fame and untimely death at the age of 22. Experience the original sound that changed rock and roll music as we know it. Lunch choices are Roasted Salmon or Three 2 oz Petite Filets. If needed, please request a vegetarian, gluten-free or vegan option. Price includes transportation, lunch and theatre ticket. (bn)

name: Theatre Camp Featuring Lion King

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 100 yrs

description: If you like to go fast on the ice, then speedskating is for you! This class follows the Learn to Speed Skate curriculum of Learn to Skate USA, so skaters should be at or above Learn to Skate Basic 4 when they begin. Skaters will be introduced to the basics of speed skating, with an emphasis on basic position, straightaway pushes, cornering and starts. These are the skating skills necessary to join the Northbrook Speed Skating Team and begin racing. Skaters may use figure skates, hockey skates or speed skates which are available for rent. Skaters must wear helmet and gloves.

Beyond sports, campers will enjoy pool time, creative recreational activities, local outings, and at least one field trip each week. It’s the ultimate mix of fun, sports, and friendship all summer long!

age_range.raw_age_text: Age At least 14 yrs but less than 16 yrs

description: The Counselor in Training (CIT) Program is designed for teens who are interested in developing leadership skills, gaining hands-on experience, and preparing for future employment opportunities. Each week begins with a training session at the Northbrook Community Center, where participants will explore topics such as leadership development, interviewing skills, activity planning, behavior management, and more. After training, CITs will be placed at one of our day camps for campers ages 5–7. There, they will assist staff with daily activities, lead games and crafts, and support campers during field trips. This unique experience allows participants to practice teamwork, responsibility, and problem-solving in a fun and supportive environment. CITs will leave the program with valuable skills that look great on a resume and may even lead to a future paid position as a camp counselor.

name: Friday Night Pickleball Boot Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: This Boot Camp features themes offering drills and specialized match play with pros. Players will be divided by level and placed four to a court with 60 minutes of drilling and 60 minutes of supervised match play. Themes include attacking the return of serve, hitting better third shot drops, varying the pace of the ball and getting to the net faster. Players need to know how to keep score as there will be supervised match play. Boot camps are appropriate Advanced Beginner/Intermediate level players.

name: Friday Night Pickleball Social Club

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Join us for exciting and engaging evenings at the Friday Night Pickleball Club! Whether you're a seasoned player or just starting out, this program offers something for everyone. Half of the gym will be dedicated to open play pickleball, where you can enjoy friendly matches, meet new people, and have fun. Courts will be available for casual games, allowing you to play at your own pace and skill level. The other half of the gym will feature a pickleball pro who is available to answer your questions, help you work on techniques, and go over rules. This is a fantastic opportunity to improve your game, learn new strategies, and get personalized tips from an expert. Light refreshments will be provided throughout the evening, ensuring you stay energized and hydrated while you play and learn. Sign up for the season and enjoy the flexibility of attending at your leisure each Friday. Whether you come every week or just occasionally, the Friday Night Pickleball Club is designed to fit your schedule and provide a welcoming environment for all participants. No Class 7/3.

name: Heritage Oaks Simulator League

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 18 yrs but less than 75 yrs

description: Compete in our indoor virtual golf league this offseason at Heritage Oaks. Full Swing Golf simulators feature the best graphics and real time ball flight on world class golf courses such as Pebble Beach, PGA National, St. Andrews Links, nine TPC Courses and more. League Format: Two-player teams will post a weekly combined gross score on six pre-determined golf courses during the regular season. All teams will play the same course conditions, with tee yardages designated for men and women. Teams will be awarded points during the regular season to earn a spot in the single elimination playoff bracket. (To qualify for the playoffs teams must complete at least 5 rounds by dates assigned) Weekly Closest to the Pin, Longest Drive and Longest Putt competitions add to the fun for all participants. A rolling handicap will be calculated during the regular season on a weekly basis using a triple bogey max, and will be applied during the playoff matches. During the playoffs each player will receive 70% of their handicap to determine the total net score. Ties will be broken using a scorecard playoff using the USGA method, last 6 holes, then last three holes, and finally the 9th hole. Regular Season: Oct. 19 - Nov 29 Playoffs: Nov 30 – Jan 10 Nine Hole Matches with a 9-Hole Championship Match League Fees: $60 per player for regular season and post season payouts, plus weekly contests (CTP, Long Drive, Long Putt) League rounds can be booked up to 14-days prior at the standard hourly simulator rental rates between 9am-8pm by calling the golf shop or on-line seven days in-advance. Enjoy the added flexibility to play any time that fits your schedule, and play rounds ahead of time as needed. Rules and Eligibility: Must be 21 years of age or older.

name: Northbrook Pickleball Co-Ed League - Intermediate

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Enjoy a fun, social and competitive league that allows you to play with a variety of players each week as you look to make your way to the top court. Register individually. Participants will play five games each week. Our leagues are categorized by skill level. We kindly request that you carefully review the description of each level and register for the one that best matches your abilities. Advanced Beginner (2.0): Players at this level understand the rules, know how to keep score, can hit forehands, backhands, and volleys, and can serve accurately. They also know where to stand when serving and returning. Low Intermediate (2.5): Players at this level know the basic rules and the two-bounce rule, can hit forehands and backhands with direction, serve accurately, sustain a dink rally, volley with some direction, understand the fundamentals, and keep score accurately. Intermediate (3.0): Players at this level can hit medium-paced forehands and backhands, serve with depth and accuracy, control a dink rally, hit medium-paced third-shot drops, and volley with direction. They understand the fundamentals of the game, positioning, and may have tournament experience. High Intermediate (3.5): Players at this level can use forehands and backhands with moderate control, consistently get serves and returns in, serve deep, and return deep. They can sustain medium-length dink rallies, control the height and depth of dink shots, and understand the variation of pace for dink shots. Advanced (4.0): Players at this level possess all the skills mentioned above and are accurate with overhead shots, can sustain dink rallies with control, height, and pace, consistently execute third-shot drops from the baseline, and can switch between soft and power shots. They can also block and return fast, hard volleys and are aware of their partner’s position on the court.

description: Northbrook Theatre Youth Company is a recreational theatre program that creates quality productions with young actors. They perform age-appropriate musicals, suitable for family viewing. name: Pickleball Co-Ed League - 60+ Intermediate

age_range.raw_age_text: 60 yrs +

description: Enjoy a fun, social and competitive league that allows you to play with a variety of players each week as you look to make your way to the top court. Register individually. Participants will play five games each week. Our leagues are categorized by skill level. We kindly request that you carefully review the description of each level and register for the one that best matches your abilities. Advanced Beginner (2.0): Players at this level understand the rules, know how to keep score, can hit forehands, backhands, and volleys, and can serve accurately. They also know where to stand when serving and returning. Low Intermediate (2.5): Players at this level know the basic rules and the two-bounce rule, can hit forehands and backhands with direction, serve accurately, sustain a dink rally, volley with some direction, understand the fundamentals, and keep score accurately. Intermediate (3.0): Players at this level can hit medium-paced forehands and backhands, serve with depth and accuracy, control a dink rally, hit medium-paced third-shot drops, and volley with direction. They understand the fundamentals of the game, positioning, and may have tournament experience. High Intermediate (3.5): Players at this level can use forehands and backhands with moderate control, consistently get serves and returns in, serve deep, and return deep. They can sustain medium-length dink rallies, control the height and depth of dink shots, and understand the variation of pace for dink shots. Advanced (4.0): Players at this level possess all the skills mentioned above and are accurate with overhead shots, can sustain dink rallies with control, height, and pace, consistently execute third-shot drops from the baseline, and can switch between soft and power shots. They can also block and return fast, hard volleys and are aware of their partner’s position on the court.

name: Pickleball Women's League - Intermediate/Advanced

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Enjoy a fun, social and competitive league that allows you to play with a variety of players each week as you look to make your way to the top court. Register individually. Participants will play five games each week. Our leagues are categorized by skill level. We kindly request that you carefully review the description of each level and register for the one that best matches your abilities. Advanced Beginner (2.0): Players at this level understand the rules, know how to keep score, can hit forehands, backhands, and volleys, and can serve accurately. They also know where to stand when serving and returning. Low Intermediate (2.5): Players at this level know the basic rules and the two-bounce rule, can hit forehands and backhands with direction, serve accurately, sustain a dink rally, volley with some direction, understand the fundamentals, and keep score accurately. Intermediate (3.0): Players at this level can hit medium-paced forehands and backhands, serve with depth and accuracy, control a dink rally, hit medium-paced third-shot drops, and volley with direction. They understand the fundamentals of the game, positioning, and may have tournament experience. High Intermediate (3.5): Players at this level can use forehands and backhands with moderate control, consistently get serves and returns in, serve deep, and return deep. They can sustain medium-length dink rallies, control the height and depth of dink shots, and understand the variation of pace for dink shots. Advanced (4.0): Players at this level possess all the skills mentioned above and are accurate with overhead shots, can sustain dink rallies with control, height, and pace, consistently execute third-shot drops from the baseline, and can switch between soft and power shots. They can also block and return fast, hard volleys and are aware of their partner’s position on the court.

name: Taekwondo - Advanced: Red - Black Belts

age_range.raw_age_text: 7 yrs +

description: Taekwondo, one of the newest Olympic sports, is a 2,000-year-old martial art, offering a variety of benefits for people of all ages and physical abilities. Students have the opportunity to improve concentration, self-esteem, achieve lifelong physical fitness, and learn self-defense skills. Classes are taught under the direction of Grand Master Ki Hong Kim (9th Dan Kukkiwon World Taekwondo Headquarters). All students should talk to their instructor on the first day to get sized for a uniform which costs $50 cash or check. Uniforms are required to complete the class and to test for belt rank. Belt testing is offered through KH Kim Taekwondo, at an additional fee. Tests happen at the instructor's discretion when the student has learned the appropriate skills. All green belt students (Ages 7 yrs and up) are required to have complete sparring gear, which is purchased from the Instructor. Students will develop heightened focus, mental discipline, and strategic thinking, while enhancing their cardiovascular conditioning, flexibility, body control, and the beginning of mastery-level material to prepare students not only to earn their black belt, but to embody the role of a martial artist at the highest level. No Class 9/7 & 9/21.

description: Step into the spotlight and join us for a seniors-only production of The Music Man SR! Participants will learn the fundamentals of putting on a musical production, including acting, singing, stage movement, character development, rehearsal techniques, and performance skills. description: Program Details Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including: Proper face and body position Survival floating Breath control As swimmers progress, instructors introduce and refine all major swim strokes, along with: Lateral breathing Deep-water treading Diving The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Safety & Participation Expectations To participate in group lessons, children must be able to: Stay with their group Follow directions from aquatic staff Remain safely above water while waiting their turn (sitting on the ledge, standing on in-water risers, or staying in designated shallow areas) Children who are unable to meet these expectations, require excessive one-on-one attention, or disrupt group safety may be removed from the class and issued a prorated refund. Private lessons may be recommended as an alternative. Refund & Makeup Policy Last day to request a refund: June 27th. In order to maintain the integrity of our classes regarding content, size, consistency and progression, we do not offer make-ups.

description: Program Details Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught <>Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including: Proper face and body position Survival floating Breath control As swimmers progress, instructors introduce and refine all major swim strokes, along with: Lateral breathing Deep-water treading Diving The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Safety & Participation Expectations To participate in group lessons, children must be able to: Stay with their group Follow directions from aquatic staff Remain safely above water while waiting their turn (sitting on the ledge, standing on in-water risers, or staying in designated shallow areas) Children who are unable to meet these expectations, require excessive one-on-one attention, or disrupt group safety may be removed from the class and issued a prorated refund. Private lessons may be recommended as an alternative. Refund Policy Last day to request a refund: July 27

name: Morning Junior Swim School 7/27-7/30 - Heritage

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: • 3-5 yrs • 30 minutes • Parents or caregivers are not allowed in the water with child. For most - it's the first time a child enters a pool without a parent so we begin by making your child feel comfortable. This may look like simply focusing on getting the face and hair wet at first, which can be scary for some. Then progressing through supported floats, bobs, kick board use, jumping in the water from side of pool, and eventually swimming 3 yards with no assistance under water. Last five minutes of class is fun time and games. POPULAR QUESTIONS: Can I sit on the pool deck and watch my child’s swim lesson? Junior Swim School is one of Arlington Heights Park District’s many “without parent” classes we offer for 3-5 year olds. Such as our ballet and gymnastics classes for this same age. These classes are intended to separate the child and parent so the teaching environment has less interruptions and improved focus to achieve better learning for all participants. If you are looking to be within arm’s reach or close enough to talk with your child during each swim lesson, please consider purchasing a Water Babies Punch Card. Parents can be in the water with their child in a Water Babies class, unlike Junior Swim School. Less interruptions and distractions from parents will allow teachers to have a more productive 30-minute lesson for everyone in their group. Help us help your child. Less interruptions. Improved focus. Better learning. My child would like specifically either a boy or girl instructor or I want a specific instructor. We recommend considering “Pop-up” Private Swim Lessons which give you the option to hand select your child’s teacher. It is not possible to select a specific instructor for group lessons. Who is teaching my child? Almost all of our instructors are currently high school or college students. Their energy is through the roof and they love their jobs and working with kids. Many are high school and college swimmers and quite a few are interested in a career specializing in early childhood and/or teaching. We aim for our swimming lesson program to be a highlight of your child’s summer! That is only possible because of our young staff. For many, this is their first job and they are eager to succeed. Can my child wear goggles? In Junior Swim School we recommend no goggles. Becoming dependent on goggles will not help your child adapt and feel comfortable in water as they grow older. Opening eyes underwater is a skill in Junior Swim School. Goggles are also not allowed on our diving boards or slides. We want your child’s first experience going off the diving board to be positive and feel familiar underwater. Often times the child who panics after going of the diving board for the first time has never felt the sensation of being underwater with no goggles. Swimming Lesson Code of Conduct – please read to make sure our program is the right fit for your family. To participate in group swimming lessons your child needs to be able to stay with their group and follow directions from all aquatic staff (instructors and lifeguards). When our swim lesson instructors are working on a skill with a child – the instructor can be up to 15 yards away from the other children in the group. Our beginner swimmers who cannot swim without assistance need to have the muscle tone and strength to do the following when it is not their turn with their instructor: 1. Sit on the ledge of the pool 2. Stand on the in-water riser if they are being used 3. Stay put, above water, in their spot in our “zero-depth”, in-water bench area, or stairs that lead into the pool. When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. When a child walks or swims away from the group, this puts every child in the group in danger. When an instructor has to take extra time to retrieve the child who has swam away, it also takes class instruction time away from everyone. If your child does not have the strength or muscle tone to stay above water when it is not their turn, is requiring excessive one-on-one attention from the instructor, or is disruptive to the other children, we will offer you a prorated refund and remove your child from the class . We will discuss other options for swim lessons to keep your child swimming safely. We do take water safety very serious and we appreciate that these policies we have in place for in-water instruction are very well received by the majority of parents. If you are unsure about your child’s ability to stay above water when it is not their turn, we do offer one-on-one private swim lesson instruction and/or coaching – with no other children in your child’s session. The last day to request a refund for this class is July 27.

name: Morning Junior Swim School 7/27-7/30 - Pioneer

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: • 3-5 yrs • 30 minutes • Parents or caregivers are not allowed in the water with child. For most - it's the first time a child enters a pool without a parent so we begin by making your child feel comfortable. This may look like simply focusing on getting the face and hair wet at first, which can be scary for some. Then progressing through supported floats, bobs, kick board use, jumping in the water from side of pool, and eventually swimming 3 yards with no assistance under water. Last five minutes of class is fun time and games. POPULAR QUESTIONS: Can I sit on the pool deck and watch my child’s swim lesson? Junior Swim School is one of Arlington Heights Park District’s many “without parent” classes we offer for 3-5 year olds. Such as our ballet and gymnastics classes for this same age. These classes are intended to separate the child and parent so the teaching environment has less interruptions and improved focus to achieve better learning for all participants. If you are looking to be within arm’s reach or close enough to talk with your child during each swim lesson, please consider purchasing a Water Babies Punch Card. Parents can be in the water with their child in a Water Babies class, unlike Junior Swim School. Less interruptions and distractions from parents will allow teachers to have a more productive 30-minute lesson for everyone in their group. Help us help your child. Less interruptions. Improved focus. Better learning. My child would like specifically either a boy or girl instructor or I want a specific instructor. We recommend considering “Pop-up” Private Swim Lessons which give you the option to hand select your child’s teacher. It is not possible to select a specific instructor for group lessons. Who is teaching my child? Almost all of our instructors are currently high school or college students. Their energy is through the roof and they love their jobs and working with kids. Many are high school and college swimmers and quite a few are interested in a career specializing in early childhood and/or teaching. We aim for our swimming lesson program to be a highlight of your child’s summer! That is only possible because of our young staff. For many, this is their first job and they are eager to succeed. Can my child wear goggles? In Junior Swim School we recommend no goggles. Becoming dependent on goggles will not help your child adapt and feel comfortable in water as they grow older. Opening eyes underwater is a skill in Junior Swim School. Goggles are also not allowed on our diving boards or slides. We want your child’s first experience going off the diving board to be positive and feel familiar underwater. Often times the child who panics after going of the diving board for the first time has never felt the sensation of being underwater with no goggles. Swimming Lesson Code of Conduct – please read to make sure our program is the right fit for your family. To participate in group swimming lessons your child needs to be able to stay with their group and follow directions from all aquatic staff (instructors and lifeguards). When our swim lesson instructors are working on a skill with a child – the instructor can be up to 15 yards away from the other children in the group. Our beginner swimmers who cannot swim without assistance need to have the muscle tone and strength to do the following when it is not their turn with their instructor: 1. Sit on the ledge of the pool 2. Stand on the in-water riser if they are being used 3. Stay put, above water, in their spot in our “zero-depth”, in-water bench area, or stairs that lead into the pool. When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. When a child walks or swims away from the group, this puts every child in the group in danger. When an instructor has to take extra time to retrieve the child who has swam away, it also takes class instruction time away from everyone. If your child does not have the strength or muscle tone to stay above water when it is not their turn, is requiring excessive one-on-one attention from the instructor, or is disruptive to the other children, we will offer you a prorated refund and remove your child from the class . We will discuss other options for swim lessons to keep your child swimming safely. We do take water safety very serious and we appreciate that these policies we have in place for in-water instruction are very well received by the majority of parents. If you are unsure about your child’s ability to stay above water when it is not their turn, we do offer one-on-one private swim lesson instruction and/or coaching – with no other children in your child’s session. The last day to request a refund for this class is July 27.

description: Program Details Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught <>Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including: Proper face and body position Survival floating Breath control As swimmers progress, instructors introduce and refine all major swim strokes, along with: Lateral breathing Deep-water treading Diving The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Safety & Participation Expectations To participate in group lessons, children must be able to: Stay with their group Follow directions from aquatic staff Remain safely above water while waiting their turn (sitting on the ledge, standing on in-water risers, or staying in designated shallow areas) Children who are unable to meet these expectations, require excessive one-on-one attention, or disrupt group safety may be removed from the class and issued a prorated refund. Private lessons may be recommended as an alternative. Refund Policy Last day to request a refund: July 27

He is joined by the Chicago Symphony Orchestra (CSO) and vocalists Micaela Diamond, Bryonha Marie, and Noah J. Ricketts. Together, they bring fresh voices and vibrant storytelling to a sweeping musical journey, unearthing beloved classics and hidden treasures that reflect the spirit, struggles, and enduring hope of America. The program shines with iconic songs and orchestral favorites, including "Summertime," "Shenandoah," "Over the Rainbow," the hoedown from Copland’s Rodeo, and many more timeless standards and contemporary anthems. Before the concert, enjoy a family-style lunch at Francesca’s North. Lunch includes an appetizer of sausage and peppers, Insalata Classica salad, Rigatoni Alla Vodka, Polo Allo Romana, and Torta di Formaggio for dessert. Our journey includes stops in Batavia, Geneva, the beautifully restored Egyptian Theatre in DeKalb, and the famous Headon’s Meat Market in Creston. Enjoy a boxed lunch, provided by Headon’s Meat Market, at the historic old Opera House in Creston. Box lunches include a choice of sandwich and salad, along with chips, fruit, a cookie, and a bottle of water. Sandwich choices: Ham & Swiss, Turkey & Cheddar, or Roast Beef & Provolone Salad choices: Potato Salad or Macaroni Salad We’ll also visit several charming small towns along the route, with time for photo opportunities, souvenir browsing, and comfortable rest breaks throughout the day. Must Register By July 15

Experience the incredible size and power of a bison herd firsthand, from the safety of a Bison Tour Wagon. The herd consists of over 100 bison and the farm provides locally grown bison meat, leather goods and hides. You can also find one-of-a-kind jewelry available for purchase in their store. After visiting the bison, enjoy lunch at Suzie’s Cafe. Lunch includes a choice of sandwich and side, along with a non-alcoholic beverage, and dessert. Sandwich choices: Cheeseburger, Grilled Chicken, BLT, or Bison Burger Side choices: French Fries, Fresh Fruit, or Homemade Potato Salad We will also stop to shop at the Albanese Confectionery, maker of the “world’s best gummy bears”, in addition chocolates and nutty treats. Must Register By July 20.

name: Ride & Glide In Wisconsin Tour - WAITLIST ONLY

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: RIDE & GLIDE IN WISCONSIN! Mid-Continent Railway Museum & Upper Dells Boat Tour Lunch at River’s Edge Pub & Grub New Freedom & Wisconsin Dells, Wisconsin Thursday, August 20, 2026 6:30 AM - 7:30 PM Trains, boats, and timeless Wisconsin scenery come together on this full-day adventure! Step back in time at the Mid-Continent Railway Museum, an outdoor living history museum celebrating the Golden Age of Railroading. Board a restored steel train coach for a scenic 55-minute, seven-mile round-trip ride through the countryside. Before the ride, explore the museum grounds filled with historic railcars, locomotives, and engaging exhibits that bring railroad history to life. Midday, enjoy lunch at River’s Edge Pub & Grub. Choose from two pieces of broasted chicken or broasted cod, served with mashed potatoes, a chef’s choice vegetable, breadstick, dessert, and a non-alcoholic beverage. A cash bar is available. Then it’s time to shift from rails to river for a two-hour guided cruise along the Wisconsin River, above the dam in Wisconsin Dells. The tour includes two exclusive shore landings. Witches Gulch, a dramatic and eerie walk through a passage carved by wind and water; and Stand Rock, a towering sandstone formation known for its legendary leap by a dog to the top.

description: BAREFOOT IN THE PARK THEATRE OF WESTERN SPRINGS LUNCH AT HILLGROVE TAP Western Springs, Illinois Saturday, September 12, 2026 10:30 AM – 5:15 PM Barefoot in the Park is a delightful romantic comedy play by Neil Simon that captures the excitement of young love. Newlyweds Corie and Paul Bratter are eager to begin their life together on the top floor of a small, run-down brownstone in New York City—without an elevator. Corie is a free-spirited optimist, while Paul is a reserved lawyer. As their contrasting expectations clash, a whirlwind of quirky neighbors and unexpected guests challenges their relationship. With sparkling humor, genuine warmth and timeless charm, the young couple learns to navigate the ups and downs of life together. Before the show, enjoy a family-style lunch at The Hillgrove Tap. The menu includes a chopped wedge salad, rigatoni pasta with Italian sausage, chicken in lemon sauce and cheesecake for dessert. Coffee, tea, and soft drinks are included. A cash bar is available.

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 12y 11m

description: Program Details: Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview: Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught: Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including proper face and body position, survival floating, and breath control.
