name: Innovation & Indulgence: A Day In Racine Tour

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: INNOVATION & INDULGENCE: A DAY IN RACINE SC JOHNSON CAMPUS TOUR LUNCH AT REEFPOINT BREW HOUSE SHOPPING AT O&H BAKERY Racine, Wisconsin Monday, September 14, 2026 8:15 AM - 4:15 PM Explore the home of SC Johnson in Racine, Wisconsin, where household brands like Pledge, Glade, Off and Windex are produced. This docent-guided walking tour combines iconic Frank Lloyd Wright architecture with a modern, eco-friendly workplace. Appreciate stunning architecture while learning about the company's history and its impact. Bring a state ID or driver’s license for tour check-in. The tour includes indoor and outdoor spaces. Guests should be comfortable standing, walking and climbing stairs. Elevators are available in Fortaleza Hall and Waxbird Commons. The Golden Rondelle Theater, Fortaleza Hall and Waxbird Commons are walker-accessible and the main floor of the Great Workroom is accessible via ramp. The Research Tower is accessible only via stairs. After the tour, enjoy lunch at Reefpoint Brew House, overlooking Racine Harbor. Lunch includes a non-alcoholic beverage and a cash bar is available. Entree choices are: Reuben (marbled rye, corned beef, Swiss cheese,1000 Island and sauerkraut) with fries Italian Bella (tomato focaccia bun, caramelized onions, grilled portobello mushroom, roasted red peppers, spinach tomatoes and pesto aioli) with fries Brew House Burger (brioche bun, lettuce, tomatoes and red onions) with fries Fisherman’s Catch (pretzel bun, fried cod, lettuce, tomatoes, red onions, pickles and tartar sauce) with fries Cobb Salad (mixed greens, bacon bits, smoked turkey, tomatoes, avocado, egg, blue cheese crumbles and choice of dressing) Following lunch, stop at O&H Danish Bakery, renowned for its savory and sweet treats, including Kringles! Purchase something delicious for dessert or to take home for later. Orders can be placed in advance at www.ohdanishbakery.com to ensure they will have what you want. When ordering and checking out, choose their Racine West location on Washington Avenue.

Any individual 8-18 years old who has an interest in diving, can swim comfortably in deep water, and dive in head first off the side of the pool deck into deep water can take this class. Students will be taught a forward approach and a back press. They will progress to forward and backward dives as well as other skills based on ability. Your child must be comfortable in deep water and be able to swim 20 yards unassisted in deep water to enroll in this class. Swimming instruction is not provided in diving lessons. All participants must become an AAU Diving Athlete member- $20. Register online at aausports.org/Join-AAU. Proof of AAU Diving registration MUST be shown on first day of class. name: Swim School

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 12y 11m

description: Program Details: Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview: Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught: Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including proper face and body position, survival floating, and breath control. As swimmers progress, instructors introduce and refine all major swim strokes, along with lateral breathing, deep-water treading, and diving. The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Refund Policy: The last day to request a refund is 2 weeks after the class start date. name: Experience Pullman!

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: EXPERIENCE PULLMAN! PULLMAN EXHIBIT HALL, BUS TOUR & VISITOR CENTER OF PULLMAN NATIONAL HISTORICAL PARK Chicago, Illinois Friday, September 25, 2026 8:30 AM - 3:30 PM Must register by September 9. Pullman is a remarkable place where American history, innovation, and community come to life. Begin at the Pullman Exhibit Hall with a short video exploring Pullman's history and its role in American industry and labor. Browse historic photographs and artifacts that bring the community's story to life. Then take a guided bus tour through the Pullman Historic District, focused on the beautifully preserved exteriors of homes and public buildings from the 1880s. Along the way, learn about the neighborhood's distinctive architecture and lasting community significance. After enjoying a boxed lunch at the Exhibit Hall, a short bus ride brings us to Pullman National Historical Park to explore the visitor center exhibits and historic grounds at your own pace. The boxed lunches include a choice of sandwich, with garden pasta salad, fresh fruit salad and a salted caramel bar for dessert. A bottle of water is also included. Please choose a first and second sandwich option, as the caterer requires specific sandwich counts. Effort will be made to provide everyone with their first choice. The sandwich choices are: Roast Beef & Cheddar Smoked Ham & Swiss Roast Turkey & Colby Jack Albacore Tuna

Kids will experience a hurricane dramatization to be sure their bridge is structurally sound! Participants may take their edible creation home or eat it on the spot! This workshop is truly the perfect blend of S.T.E.M. meets Kid’s Life Coaching. Instructor: Lisa Lombardi Coaching Inc, www.lisalombardi.com. Drop your child off class. (CH)

Join us at the House of Gerhard for authentic German cuisine in an enchanting atmosphere filled with old-world charm. Lunch includes a choice of entrée, Chicken Spaetzle soup, homemade German hard rolls, sweet muffins and their signature dessert, the Strawberry Schaum Torte. Entrée options are: Bavarian Pot Roast: Tender sliced beef topped with brown gravy, served with red cabbage and mashed potatoes Roast Loin of Pork: Juicy center-cut pork with sage dressing and pork gravy, served with vegetables and mashed potatoes Roasted Chicken Breast: Boneless chicken breast with herb stuffing, served with vegetables and mashed potatoes Coffee, tea, and milk are included. A cash bar is available. After lunch, visit Mars Cheese Castle, a Wisconsin institution. Mars Cheese Castle features a specialty market offering more than 700 cheeses, wines and specialty items; an in-house bakery with desserts, kringles and freshly baked bread; as well as a pub known for its Wisconsin beers and famous Bloody Marys.

description: CHICAGO SPORTS LEGENDS & LANDMARK! SOLDIER FIELD TOUR & CHICAGO SPORTS MUSEUM LUNCH AT HARRY CARAY’S 7TH INNING STRETCH Monday, October 12, 2026 8:45 AM - 4:30 PM Go behind-the-scenes at Soldier Field! Since its founding in 1924, Soldier Field has served as a symbol of tradition and excellence, honoring the men and women of the armed services. Today, it is the home of the Chicago Bears (NFL) and the Chicago Fire FC (MLS). Whether you're a die-hard sports fan or a history enthusiast, this tour offers you unprecedented access to the heart of the action! Then take a lunch break at Harry Caray’s 7th Inning Stretch. Lunch includes a choice of entree, a mixed baby greens salad, a funfetti cupcake and a non-alcoholic beverage station. Entree choices are: Short Rib Italian Beef Sandwich with Provolone, giardiniera, au jus, Parmesan & Romano cheese, garlic bread and french fries Chinese Chicken Salad with Chinese long beans, toasted cashews, napa cabbage, sesame seeds, carrots, wontons, mandarin oranges and sesame soy dressing Turkey Burger with roasted roma tomato, baby spinach, smoked mozzarella, basil pesto, red wine vinaigrette, brioche bun and french fries A cash bar is available. After lunch, visit The Chicago Sports Museum. This museum combines high-tech interactive experiences with unique sports memorabilia and an impressive collection of game-used treasures and artifacts. The 23,000-square-foot space celebrates all of Chicago's major sports teams.

name: Jailhouse Rock In Joliet Tour

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: JAILHOUSE ROCK IN JOLIET! OLD JOLIET PRISON & ILLINOIS ROCK & ROLL MUSEUM SELF-PAY LUNCH AT PROTILLO'S IN SHOREWOOD Joliet & Shorewood, Illinois Wednesday, October 21, 2026 8:45 AM - 5:00 PM This 90-minute walking tour of the Old Joliet Prison is led by knowledgeable docents and tour guides from the Joliet Area Historical Museum. The tour provides an overview of the prison's history, from its opening in 1858 to its closure in 2002. Explore various historic buildings throughout the 16-acre prison site and hear fascinating accounts of prison life, notable inmates, escapes and the evolution of the facility. The Joliet Prison tour is entirely outdoors, rain or shine. The tour covers a considerable distance with some areas not fully paved or in poor condition. Please dress appropriately for the weather and wear comfortable walking or hiking shoes.. After touring the prison, we will stop for a quick self-pay lunch at Portillo’s in Shorewood. Bring money for lunch. Following lunch, tour The Illinois Rock & Roll Museum, which celebrates the rich musical legacy of Illinois and its significant impact on rock and roll history. The museum honors legendary artists, producers and industry influencers. As a cultural hub on the iconic Route 66, the museum connects generations through music, preserving the stories and sounds that have shaped America’s musical landscape.

description: Join the Park District's annual Trunk or Treat event on Saturday, 10/24, from 10a-12:30pm at Pioneer Park, 500 S. Fernandez Ave. This family-friendly event celebrates Halloween by providing a unique way for children ages 2-13 to trick-or-treat with parental supervision. Participating organizations have the opportunity to introduce and publicize their brand to participating families in a festive atmosphere while providing a fun service to the community. Registration is free and includes parking for one sedan to SUV sized vehicle. To ensure that your vehicle is event-ready and on-theme and that the treat line moves safely and smoothly: Come in costume and decorate your vehicle in a Halloween theme of your choice. Bring Halloween handouts (packaged candy or toy) for 1,000 children. You may also pass out a coupon for your business, but this must be in addition to your Halloween treat. We do not provide tables, chairs, or access to electricity, so be sure to bring any supplies you may need. All supplies, including decorations and signage, must fit in/ slightly in front of two standard parking spaces. Generators, music that projects beyond the immediate area of your vehicle, and games that slow the trick-or-treat line are not allowed. Access to the parking lot opens at 8:30am and closes at 9:30am. Late vehicles will not be allowed in the lot. If your organization would like to have a larger Trunk or Treat impact, contact Amy Lewandowski, Director of Marketing, at alewandowski@ahpd.org, to inquire about limited sponsorship opportunities for this event.

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: THE GREAT LAKE COUNTY GHOST ADVENTURE SITES AROUND LAKE COUNTY ILLINOIS LUNCH AT RIVALRY ALEHOUSE IN ANTIOCH Thursday, October 29, 2026 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM Participate in a 7-hour paranormal journey led by an experienced paranormal researcher. Visit cemeteries, historic landmarks, and notorious haunted sites where ghostly legends still linger. Experience Lake County's most chilling tales firsthand, including phantom apparitions on Cuba Road and the mysteries of the Genesee Theatre. Enjoy a spaghetti and meatball lunch at Rivalry Alehouse in Antioch. The lunch includes a salad and soft drinks. A cash bar will be available. A cookie treat will be provided during the trip. Wear comfortable shoes and dress appropriately for the weather, as many of the stops will be outdoors and involve some walking. Don't forget to bring your cameras and any ghost hunting tools you may have, or feel free to try out theirs!

You will be asked to attend our mandatory coaches meeting 1 week prior to the start of the season. Questions? Please email Laura Husko, Athletics Supervisor, at Lhusko@ahpd.org or review our FAQs for Players/Parents . (LH)

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 12y 11m

description: Program Details: Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview: Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught: Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including proper face and body position, survival floating, and breath control. As swimmers progress, instructors introduce and refine all major swim strokes, along with lateral breathing, deep-water treading, and diving. name: Swim School

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 12y 11m

description: Program Details: Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview: Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught: Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including proper face and body position, survival floating, and breath control. As swimmers progress, instructors introduce and refine all major swim strokes, along with lateral breathing, deep-water treading, and diving. The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Refund Policy: The last day to request a refund is 2 weeks after the class start date. age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 8 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: Level 1 The beginner diving class is an introduction to the sport of springboard diving and is designated to teach the safe and proper way to use the springboard. Any individual 8-18 years old who has an interest in diving, can swim comfortably in deep water, and dive in head first off the side of the pool deck into deep water can take this class. Students will be taught a forward approach and a back press. They will progress to forward and backward dives as well as other skills based on ability. Your child must be comfortable in deep water and be able to swim 20 yards unassisted in deep water to enroll in this class. Swimming instruction is not provided in diving lessons. All participants must become an AAU Diving Athlete member- $20. Register online at aausports.org/Join-AAU. Proof of AAU Diving registration MUST be shown on first day of class. All diving lessons are video recorded.

name: Holiday Cheer

age_range.raw_age_text: 21 yrs +

description: HOLIDAY CHEER Code 99115 Friday, December 11 11AM-3PM Cotillion Banquets, 360 S. Creekside Drive, Palatine $55 per person Celebrate the holiday season with your friends from AHPD! Enjoy a festive afternoon at The Cotillion with a sit-down lunch, live entertainment and two exciting raffles! The Traditional Raffle features gift cards, local goods, and experience prizes. Raffle opens pre-event at the Senior Center on November 12. Winners need not be present at Holiday Cheer. The Split the Pot raffle gives one winner 50% of total Split the Pot ticket sales. Tickets are sold at Holiday Cheer. Winner must be present to win. MENU: Starter: Minestrone soup Entrée Choices: Filet of Salmon with parisienne potatoes, key west vegetable blend Chicken Vesuvio with parisienne potatoes, key west vegetable blend Roast Loin of Pork with parisienne potatoes, key west vegetable blend Vegetable Brochette Kabob with rice (vegan) Dessert: Ice cream parfait Beverages: Soda, coffee and tea included. Cash bar available for alcoholic beverages. No food substitutions allowed, but please alert staff of any food allergies upon registration. DETAILS: Registration not available day of the event. Registrants will be assigned a table upon sign up. To reserve multiple seats at a table, all registration and payments must be submitted at the same time. Doors open at 11AM. For any accessibility inquiries, please call 847.797.5341. This is a contracted program; non-refundable upon registration. TO REGISTER: Call 847.797.5341 or visit AHPD at the Senior Center

name: Glitzy Girlz: Parent/Child Annual Holiday Gift Memories 2026

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 10y 11m

description: Come join Glitzy Girlz (www.glitzygirlz.com) to attend our most treasured holiday gift class. Each couple will be teaming up to make special hand-made gifts for family and friends. They will make and take home (3) personalized gifts consisting of crafts and a jewelry piece. The gifts can be made for girls and boys of all ages and a large variety of beads display. Each couple will also get supplies to make gifts bags, tags and tissue to conceal the holiday surprises! You MUST attend this most special memory of 2026 with your kids! **DROP OFF CLASS** Parents are not allowed to stay in class due to space and activities.

name: Grinch Goo-tastic Holiday Slime Lab - Life Coaching For Kids

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13y 11m

description: Kids will have the slime of their life creating seasonal Grinch inspired slime. We will develop the skill of perseverance as we take the steps and patience needed to form stretchy slime. Our concoction lab will include all the colors of Christmas, Grinch hearts, seasonal mix ins, along with winter scents that will make you feel like you are in the Grinch story! Imagine your slime smelling like a holiday firepit, fragrant pine trees, candy canes, or a box of holiday chocolates. We will also play a slimy game to catch the Grinch before he steals our Christmas. This is crazy FUN to blow off some steam as kids get excited for winter break to arrive. Every participant will go home with the slime they made. Instructor: Lisa Lombardi Coaching Inc., www.lisalombardi.com. Drop your child off class. (CH)

name: Lathe Bottle Stopper Workshop

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Learn woodturning and create a one-of-a-kind bottle stopper in this hands-on workshop! Learn the basics of using a lathe to shape and finish this unique, functional piece. All materials provided. No experience needed. (AV)

name: Family Gingerbread House Decorating

age_range.raw_age_text: 5 yrs +

description: Helping to continue a well-loved tradition, families will receive all of the materials to build their very own gingerbread house! Hopefully you use more candy then you eat as you decorate as much or as little as you'd like with an assortment of candy provided. No baking necessary for this program, just show up, have fun and get creative. Register ONE family member - fee listed is the per family rate. (JL)

name: Winter Express to Harvard 9:15am train

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 2 yrs but less than 100 yrs

location: METRA TRAIN: Downtown AH to Harvard
description: All aboard our Storytime Train! On the train to and from Harvard, our conductor will read the Polar Express storybook, and we'll enjoy music, a snack, and a special visit from Santa. The event begins and ends at the Arlington Heights Train Station in downtown Arlington Heights: train departs from AH at 9:15am and returns to AH at 11:30am. Please note! This activity is recommended primarily for children ages 3 to 10 years. So that we may include as many children as possible, we kindly ask no more than 2 adults per family register. Regardless of age, everyone who is riding on the train must pre-register and all children must be accompanied by a registered adult. If you register your child without an adult, they may lose their spot on the train. On-site registration will not be available. Strollers and pets are not allowed on the train. If registration fills before you are able to register all of the members of your family, please register additional family members on the wait list. We manage this wait list carefully and make every effort to include as many passengers as are allowed. Refunds will only be issued for withdrawal requests submitted via our website or in writing to Cari Boyle, Events Supervisor, at cboyle@ahpd.org, by Sunday, 12/6/26, and are subject to a $5 transaction fee per registration. (CB)

Class is open to individuals and couples. We recommend that you avoid wearing gym shoes to sessions so you can turn smoothly on the floor.

Gather your friends and raise a glass as we celebrate our 40th Garden to Glass! Parking is available at St. Matthew's Church.

Fee includes one kit per team and free admission to the event. All kits must be picked up from the Farm Visitor Center on November 14th between 11-3pm. Each team will recieve one kit. age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: Forest Therapy is a research-based framework for supporting healing and wellness through immersion in forests and other natural environments. Often translated as “forest bathing,” it is rooted in the Japanese practice of Shinrin-Yoku. Your guide, trained by The Forest Therapy School, will lead you through a series of gentle invitations and meditation that will help you find a deeper connection with the natural world. Park and meet at St. Matthew’s Church entrance (1001 E. Schaumburg Rd.).

name: Hip Hop Adult

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Hip-Hop is a high intensity dance form that is often paired with the latest hip-hop music. Having evolved from “street dancing”, hip-hop has an edgy component which is taught through isolations of the body in addition to alternating between smooth and quick, sharp movements. This class will increase flexibility and coordination by challenging the pace at which the dancer’s body can move. This class helps express personality through movement that allows for a little attitude.

name: Intro to Contemporary

age_range.raw_age_text: 6 yrs +

description: Contemporary is a merging of both ballet and jazz styles of dance, combining jazz skills with the ease and gracefulness of ballet. This style of dance focuses on an emotional connection to the lyrics of a song and expressing that through movement. This challenges the student to connect on a deeper level to the dance and to become a part of the music.

name: A Christmas Carol - Paramount Theatre

price.raw_price_text: Resident Fee: If Resident for Customer: $59.00; Non-Resident Fee: If Non-resident for Customer: $64.00

age_range.raw_age_text: 21 yrs +

description: Rediscover the magic of the holiday season with A Christmas Carol, the timeless tale that warms hearts and reminds us all of the true spirit of Christmas. Ebenezer Scrooge, a bitter and lonely miser, is visited on Christmas Eve by three ghosts who take him on a journey through his past, present, and future. Along the way, he learns how to once again experience joy, compassion, and the power of generosity. Whether you’re experiencing Scrooge’s transformation for the first time or reliving the magic of the classic story once again, this play enriched with live music will leave you filled with hope and holiday cheer. Fee includes transportation and main floor seating at the Paramount Theatre. Registration deadline is October 26. (AS)

name: AARP Smart Driver Course

age_range.raw_age_text: 55 yrs +

description: Tune up your driving skills and drive more safely. Seniors 55+ with clean driving records may be eligible to receive an insurance discount upon course completion. This is an eight-hour course and those registered are required to attend both days. Pre-registration is required. A $20 fee AARP member/$25 fee non-AARP member needs to be paid by check payable to AARP and brought to class the first day. You will also need to bring your AARP member number and DL number. (AS)

name: Accessible Transportation Options

age_range.raw_age_text: 21 yrs +

description: Accessible Metra, Pace and CTA buses and trains are easy to use and the Northern Illinois Transit Authority (NITA - formerly RTA) would love to show you how! It is important that older adults and people with disabilities stay informed about accessible public transportation options and traveling independently. Topics covered will include: local public transportation options, accessibility features on CTA, Pace, and Metra, NITA's reduced fare and ride free programs, travel safety tips, and Q&A sessions with a NITA Representative. Help will also be available for those wanting to apply for transportation cards that day. Don't miss this NITA Group Transit Orientation Presentation. Free to attend but pre-registration is encouraged. Call (630) 993-8193 to reserve your spot. (AS)

description: Delve into the history and mechanics of your favorite amusement park rides in this imaginative unit. Students will use our proprietary LEGO® technic kits to construct a Ferris Wheel, Carousel Swing, Swing Boat Ride, and a Merry Go Round. Our one-of-a-kind kits incorporate beams, axles, gears, motors & battery packs to make our creations come to life! Lessons incorporate principles of physics, described in a way children can understand, such as “G-force” inertia and momentum, as well as math concepts. These engaging lessons will give students an understanding of the physical forces they experience every day. (BS)

description: CAMP CANTEEN campers should be entering 6th, 7th or 8th Grade in Fall 2026. Camp Canteen is the perfect active day camp for kids entering 6th-8th grade! Our experienced, enthusiastic and highly trained staff lead your child through a safe and engaging summer. We have small groups, low camper to staff ratios and great indoor and outdoor spaces for well-planned activities. Canteen campers will swim at our outdoor pools twice a week and attend two field trips each week. Before and after camp care is also available for those who need an extended day. description: Celebrate Lucille Ball's birthday with a sweet and nostalgic day dedicated to everyone's favorite redhead! Our day begins at Long Grove Confectionery, where we'll learn all about the art of chocolate making, tour the production line, and enjoy time to sample and shop in the outlet store. Next, we'll indulge in a Cuban-themed lunch featuring chicken skewers over rice, roasted vegetables, rolls & butter, salad, and dessert. After lunch, we'll head to University Center for a special presentation by Todd Hunt, who will take us on a journey back to the golden age of television. Through engaging slides, audio, and video clips, we'll explore how "I Love Lucy" was created and discover fascinating stories about Lucy, Desi, and their castmates. This fun-filled day is the perfect way to honor what would have been Lucy's 115th birthday! Fee includes motor coach transportation, factory tour, lunch, and private presentation by Todd Hunt. Registration deadline is July 15. (AS)

description: The Elmhurst Park District invites you to honor a loved one or commemorate a special occasion with a permanent engraved brick paver. Pavers are ordered four times per year. The following are the cut-off dates for orders and the approximate date of installation: Order in By Installed By July 1st October 1st October 1st January 1st (weather permitting) January 1st April 1st (weather permitting) April 1st July 1st The dates above allow enough time for shipping and installation of pavers at the walk. Winter orders are installed as soon as the ground thaws. On occasion, the engraving company will be extremely busy and additional time will have to be allowed for engraving and delivery. In this hands-on program, little artists and their grown-ups will decorate their very own small pumpkin using paint, stickers, googly eyes, glitter, and more. This is a not-so-spooky, mess-friendly way to celebrate the season—no carving involved, just colorful, crafty fun! (CB) Registration Deadline: October 10

name: Family Science Night

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: Get ready for a night of ooey-gooey, fizz-tastic fun at Family Science Night! Stretch, squish, and swirl your way through our Slime Station, stand back in amazement as Elephant Toothpaste erupts in a foamy explosion, and snap a silly pic in the science-themed photo booth complete with goggles and props. Jump into hands-on science games and experiments that spark curiosity, giggles, and “WOW!” moments for all ages - because learning science is way more fun when the whole family gets to play together!(CB) Fee is per person. Please register everyone attending. Children must be accompanied by an adult. This is not a drop off event.

name: Friday Friendventures: A Character Exploration

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: Friday Morning Adventures is an engaging preschool class where children explore a different popular character each week. From superheroes and princesses to animals and explorers, each theme comes to life through crafts, stories, music, and movement activities. In a fun and supportive environment, children build creativity, social skills, and confidence while making new friends and learning through play. Every Friday morning is a new adventure filled with imagination, laughter, and hands-on fun! We will be having a themed snack so please make us aware of any allergies. Bring a filled, labeled water bottle to class. (CB)

name: From River to Roastery - A Day Exploring Chicago

age_range.raw_age_text: 21 yrs +

description: This day trip offers an engaging exploration of some of Chicago’s most unique urban attractions. Participants will begin at Chicago’s Wild Mile, the world’s first floating eco-park, where they can experience innovative river restoration efforts, enjoy scenic views, and learn about local ecology and sustainability initiatives on a guided tour. The trip continues to Washington Hall, a vibrant culinary destination featuring a variety of local vendors and diverse cuisines, for lunch on your own. The day concludes at the iconic Starbucks Reserve Roastery, where participants can experience small-batch coffee roasting, specialty beverages, and the immersive design of one of Starbucks’ flagship locations. This program blends environmental education, cultural exploration, and culinary discovery for a memorable Chicago experience. Trip includes transportation and guided tour of the Wild Mile. Purchases at Washington Hall and Starbucks Reserve Roastery are on your own. Registration deadline is September 1. (AS)

name: Full STEAM Ahead

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: Explore gravity and force by knocking things down with a pendulum and setting off chain reactions. Plan and build structures, conduct experiments, investigate living things, and learn how to work as a team. This action-packed class will prove that your STEAM investigator can be an engineer, biologist, chemist, and mathematician all while having fun! Topic of the week and activities are the same in both the Monday and Wednesday classes. (CB)

name: Fun Fall Wreaths

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 10 yrs

description: Celebrate the season together in our Fun Fall Wreaths class! Caregivers and children will team up to design and decorate a beautiful autumn wreath using colorful leaves, seasonal accents, and creative touches. This hands-on class is full of creativity, teamwork, and festive fun as families craft a one-of-a-kind decoration to take home. Enjoy quality time, make special memories, and welcome fall with a project you’ll be proud to display! (CB)

name: Funseekers Day Camp North: 1st Grade - RED POD

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 7 yrs

description: RED POD campers should be entering 1st Grade in Fall 2026. Funseekers Day Camp is THE go-to camp for an exciting summer of fun! Let our experienced, enthusiastic and highly trained staff lead your child through a safe and engaging summer. We have small groups, low camper to staff ratios and great indoor and outdoor spaces for many well-planned activities. Campers swim at our outdoor pools two times a week and attend one field trip a week. Before & after camp care is also available for children needing an extended day. (TGR) All campers should bring a sack lunch, water bottle, towel, and sunscreen every day. There is no camp on July 3. Drop off in the morning is between 8:45-9:15 A.M. A $100 deposit per child per week will be charged at time of registration. WITHDRAWAL/REFUND POLICY: In the event you need to cancel a camp, please do so immediately. Withdrawals can be done online through your online account or by submitting at Camp Withdrawal Form (https://www.epd.org/programs/camps) to the registration office at registration@epd.org, or by calling 630-993-8900. A $25 cancellation fee will apply to refunds for each session of camp that costs over $175, and a $10 cancellation fee for camps less than $175. Refund requests for camps must be received 10 business days or more prior to the start of camp to be eligible for a refund. Refunds requested within 10 business days of the start of camp will be considered only for injury or illness with a doctor's note before the camp begins.

name: Garden Plots

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: REGISTRATION FOR NEW GARDENERS STARTS MARCH 19 at 8 am! Grow your own produce in an approximately 20' X 20' Elmhurst Garden Plot at Marjorie Davis Park. The Park District will rototill and stake each area, you plant, cultivate and reap the harvest. Six water taps are available and are open 9 am - 9 pm, seven days a week. Weather permitting, growing season runs from May - November 1. A maximum of one garden plot per family is allowed. RETURNING PARTICIPANTS: We will continue to give returning customers (those who had plots in 2025) the option of keeping the same plot or entering the lottery for a new plot. Returning participants must register between February 21-March 13 to secure a plot for 2026. NEW PARTICIPANTS: Those who did not have a plot in 2025 WILL BE ABLE TO REGISTER BETWEEN MARCH 19 (Beginning at 8 am) AND APRIL 5 for any available plots. Available plots will be sold on a first come first served basis. A lottery will be held for plot selection. New gardeners that get a plot will receive more information on how the lottery to choose your plot works after April 5. The lottery for plot selection will be held on Wednesday, April 15 at 6:30 pm at the Kies Recreation Center. (AS)

All levels are welcome. Great for stretching and de-stressing. You don't have to be a yogi to take this class. Participants should bring a yoga or exercise mat to class. (AS)

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: The focus of this 55-minute class is on the development of gymnastics skills on vault, bars, beam and floor. On vault, students will learn how to run and jump on the springboard, working on a good stick landing. On bars the focus is basic hanging and support skills. On balance beam, posture, balance and a variety of basic skills will be introduced. On floor the focus will be rolls, cartwheels, handstands and jumps. (KG)

We believe that gymnastics teaches life skills along with the greatest overall body conditioning your child could be involved in. Properly taught gymnastics teaches, self-motivation, self-discipline, pride, dedication, determination, work ethic, time management, teamwork, team spirit, leadership, sportsmanship, respect for others, poise, and grace. The competitive program is invitation only. (KG)

description: Our Girls Developmental Program focuses on advanced tumbling and equipment skills, with emphasis on progressive skills leading to the competitive gymnastics level. The gymnast is also introduced to dance elements in the gymnastics setting. At this level, self discipline and internal motivation become emerging benefits for the athlete. The goal is for the gymnast to eventually move into our competitive team once skills and techniques are mastered. This program is by invitation only. (KG)

Campers will be divided into groups with no more than six participants assigned to one instructor, this will be your child's instructor for the week. It is mandatory that gymnasts dress appropriately; a leotard and shorts/pants or tight fitting t-shirt and shorts/pants-hair tied back. A Sound Bath, or Sound Meditation, is a deep immersion in sound that is felt in your whole being. Find a comfortable seat or lie down and allow the soothing vibrations of singing bowls, flutes, and chimes to wash over your whole body, creating a gentle yet deeply transformative effect on your body and mind. age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: In this fun and interactive tabla course, students explore the vibrant rhythms of Hindustani classical music while learning to play this dynamic pair of hand drums. Through clapping games, spoken bols (rhythmic syllables), and hands-on drumming, participants build coordination, creativity, and confidence. No experience needed - just bring your curiosity and get ready to make some exciting rhythms! Your instructor, Bindu Pathak, has her masters in Tabla and has performed in solo competitions and with groups at temple. Each participant will need a set of Tabla drums which will be available to rent from the instructor for $12 for the session on the first night of class. (AS)

name: Tai Chi

Students may choose to sit or stand as needed, making this class suitable for all ages and abilities. (AS)

name: Tai Chi

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

Recommended for overall wellness, Tai Chi practice can help with balance, alignment, and stress reduction. Participants may also experience improved mood, increased energy, reduced chronic pain, improved sleep, and improved flexibility, balance, agility, muscle strength and definition. (AS)

name: Tai Chi in the Park

description: Step back in time and celebrate 100 years of America’s Mother Road on this comfortable, fully guided Route 66 motorcoach bus tour filled with nostalgia, history, and classic roadside charm. We begin at the Joliet Area Historical Museum , where we’ll pick up our tour guide, Ed . Along the way, we’ll visit the Elwood Arsenal Wayside and the Midewin Tallgrass Prairie Visitor Center . Photo stops include the famous Gemini Giant and the colorful Polka Dot Diner . In Gardner , we’ll see the old two-cell jail , Old Streetcar Diner , and stop at The Shop on 66 for local Route 66 history. Lunch is at the classic Old Route 66 Diner , followed by a stop at the restored gas station in Odell . We’ll finish the day in Pontiac with time for walking, shopping, and visits to the Route 66 Suspension Bridge and Old Sheriff’s Building . Tour, lunch, and transportation included. RT 66.

name: Charleston, SC Diamond Tours

age_range.raw_age_text: 30 yrs +

description: Day 1: Depart your group's location in a spacious, video and restroom equipped motorcoach as you head for your destination: Charleston, South Carolina! This evening you will stay at an en route hotel. Day 2: Enjoy a Continental Breakfast. Today you will continue your journey, then enjoy a leisurely Dinner and check into a Charleston area hotel for a four night stay. Day 3: After a Continental Breakfast, you'll head to historic MIDDLETON PLACE. This impressive attraction contains 65 acres of America's oldest landscaping. After each member receives their welcome map, you'll experience the garden, animal stables, the Chapel, Rice Mill, and more! After lunch on your own and free time in Downtown Charleston, you'll enjoy a scenic HARBOR CRUISE. Enjoy the beauty of the Charleston Harbor and learn the rich history of the "Holy City". During this scenic and relaxing tour, you will see dozens of landmarks and points of interest as hundreds of years of history is covered. This evening, enjoy Dinner before heading back to your hotel for a good night's rest. Day 4: After a Continental Breakfast, you'll enjoy a GUIDED TOUR of McLeod Plantation Historic Site. Established in 1851, this important 37-acre Gullah/Geechee heritage site has been carefully preserved in recognition of its cultural and historical significance. Later, you'll enjoy lunch on your own in the “cultural heart of Charleston.” Next, you'll have some free time to explore The Historic Charleston City Market. Located downtown, this architecturally significant National Historic Landmark is home to eclectic shops, you won't find anywhere else. This continuous series of market buildings stretches four city blocks. Next you'll appreciate a short photo stop at the famed Angel Oak Tree, estimated to be 400 years old! This evening, enjoy Dinner before heading back to your hotel for a good night's rest. Day 5: After a Continental Breakfast, you'll enjoy both a GUIDED TOUR OF CHARLESTON and an intimate TOUR inside the HISTORIC CHARLESTON HOME: The Joseph Manigault House. The Manigault's descent from French Huguenots who fled religious persecution in Europe in the late 1600s. Afterwards, you'll visit the CHARLESTON TEA GARDEN. At this unique tea garden, your group will take a factory tour and see how tea is made, including tasting samples at the Tea Bar. A highlight of your tour includes a TROLLEY TOUR of the garden. schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Tuesday, June 9 2026. Beginning II students are required to have taken at least 1 year of consec- utive Beginning (school-age) Gymnastics classes or have had experience in a similar level with another program. They should be able to do a vertical handstand, cartwheel, and roundoff, handstand bridge kickover off a mat, a dive roll vault, and a pullover on bars with a light spot or mat against the wall. They should have experience working on handstands, cartwheels, and dismounts on beam but do not need to be able to do them unassisted. For a complete list of skills, strength, and flexibility requirements or an evaluation please email gymnastics@cityofevanston.org.

Schedule: Wednesday, 6:00 PM - 8:30 PM , Dempster Beach Launch Facility , Location: Dempster Beach Launch Facility | 1251 Lake Shore Boulevard, Evanston, IL, 60202 Description: Enjoy a beautiful summer evening with a sunset paddle on the water! After some time on Lake Michigan, you will be greeted back on land with a crackling bonfire. Kick back in our comfy Adirondack chairs, enjoy some music by the fire, and indulge in all the s’mores you can eat! All kayaking equipment and s’mores fixings are included. Children under the age of 10 must be on a kayak or paddleboard with an adult at all times.

name: Growing Healthy Minds

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Friday, August 14 2026. Schedule: Friday, 12:00 PM - 2:00 PM , Levy Center Courtyard , Location: Levy Center Courtyard (Levy Senior Center) | 300 Dodge Avenue, Evanston, IL, 60202 Description: An interactive workshop exploring the science behind gardening, movement, and wellness. name: Juneteenth Celebration

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Friday, June 19 2026. Schedule: Friday, 12:00 PM - 4:00 PM , Dawes Park , Location: Dawes Park | 1700 Sheridan Road, Evanston, IL, 60201 Description: This year's "Youthful" Juneteenth Celebration will be a community event that honors the historical legacy of Juneteenth while bringing people together in a spirit of unity, culture, and joy. The celebration recognizes the historic moment in 1865 when the last enslaved African Americans in Galveston, Texas, learned of their freedom and reflects on the continued journey toward freedom and equality for all Americans. This inclusive event welcomes people of all ages and backgrounds to celebrate through vibrant music, dancing, and cultural performances. Making community connections while supporting local food and artisan vendors. Through shared experiences, the Juneteenth Celebration creates a space to honor freedom for all, celebrate multiculturalism, and strengthen the community.

name: Counselor in Training (Robert Crown)

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Monday, June 8 2026. Schedule: Weekdays, 9:00 AM - 4:00 PM , From June 8, 2026 until July 2, 2026 , Robert Crown Gym , Location: Robert Crown Gym (Robert Crown Community Center) | 1801 Main Street, Evanston, IL, 60202 Description: Counselor in Training (CIT) Camp prepares teens to work with staff and contribute their talents to the programs offered at the Robert Crown Community Center. Participants serve as role models for the younger children, and receive weekly training from a variety of social service professionals and mentors. The program builds community and prepares youth to work with children in a variety of settings. CIT participants receive basic training on a range of topics: effective engagement, behavior management, communication, team work, safety procedures and more. Senior staff evaluate and mentor the participants throughout the four-week program and provide a final evaluation. After training and observations, CIT participants will be assigned to volunteer at camp, based on an interview and personal interests, while also receiving training on the various topics listed above. Volunteer options include Fun Factory (ages 5-7), or Kid City (ages 7-10). Volunteers are expected to participate in the program Monday through Friday, 9am-4pm for the entire four-week period. Volunteers may speak with the Camp Director to adjust their schedule if necessary. The registration fee includes training and supplies, field trips, and small group activities. Eligible for childcare tax credit. Please note that there is no class on the following date(s): Friday, June 19, 2026 from 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM

name: Session 1: Prairies

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Monday, June 8 2026. Schedule: Every day, 9:00 AM - 3:00 PM , From June 8, 2026 until June 18, 2026 , Lincolnwood Elementary , Resource person: Margaret Isaacson Location: Lincolnwood Elementary | 2600 Colfax Street, Evanston, IL, 60201 Description: Adventure awaits! Our camp for ages 5-7 brings together hands-on science, creative projects, and plenty of outdoor fun. Each session is centered around a different world biome - from deserts to rainforests to oceans - so campers can dive into the plants, animals, and unique features of each habitat. Kids enjoy a full lineup of activities - crafting, nature hikes, kid-friendly science experiments, outdoor games, and imaginative play - designed to bring each biome to life. With a sunny beach day and special field trip in the mix each session, every day offers a new opportunity to explore, learn and play in the great outdoors. This session, campers will discover the amazing plants and animals that thrive in grasslands and the clever ways they survive. Then we'll explore the unique species that call Illinois prairies home. Eligible for childcare tax credit.

name: Youth Aquatic Camp - Morning

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Monday, July 27 2026. Schedule: Every day, 9:30 AM - 12:30 PM , From July 27, 2026 until August 7, 2026 , Dempster Beach Launch Facility , Resource person: Katie Grundin kgrundin@cityofevanston.org Location: Dempster Beach Launch Facility | 1251 Lake Shore Boulevard, Evanston, IL, 60202 Description: Dive into summer fun at our Aquatic Camp! Campers will rotate through sailing, kayaking, paddleboarding, and tubing, with activities changing based on the day and weather conditions. When they’re not out on the water, they’ll stay active with games like Nukem, capture the flag, relay races, and sandcastle competitions. Please only register for a morning or afternoon session during the same dates. You may register for multiple sessions throughout the summer. Campers are required to pass a 50-yard swim test (any combination of strokes) before they may participate in aquatic activities. Refunds will not be provided if campers are unable to pass the test. Aquatic Camp meets every day, but bad weather, poor conditions or equipment failure may require that activities take place on the sand, a park, or inside the Beach Office. Eligible for childcare tax credit. Please note that there is no class on the following date(s): Saturday, August 01, 2026 from 9:30 AM to 12:30 PM Sunday, August 02, 2026 from 9:30 AM to 12:30 PM

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Monday, August 3 2026. name: Camp FLIGHT (Week 1: Aviation)

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Monday, June 8 2026. Schedule: Every day, 9:00 AM - 4:00 PM , From June 8, 2026 until June 12, 2026 , Gibbs-Morrison Cafe , Resource person: Harrington Gibson Location: Gibbs-Morrison Cafe (Gibbs-Morrison Cultural Center) | 1823 Church Street, Evanston, IL, 60201 Description: The Maccstream STEM and Aviation module offers Camp Flight participants a focused, hands-on experience where science, technology, engineering, and mathematics come to life through real application. Over the course of one week, students explore core concepts in physics and aerodynamics, use block coding to animate characters and program drones, and engage with flight simulators to understand the mechanics of aviation. They are introduced to different engineering pathways and challenged to design and build solutions that meet specific criteria, all while using practical math skills—measurement, geometry, probability, and algebra—to complete meaningful tasks. Beyond technical exposure, the experience builds problem-solving, critical thinking, and confidence. Students learn how to approach challenges with structure and creativity, while gaining insight into real-world careers in STEM and aviation. name: Camp FLIGHT (Week 2: Debate)

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Monday, June 15 2026. Schedule: Every day, 9:00 AM - 4:00 PM , From June 15, 2026 until June 18, 2026 , Gibbs-Morrison Cafe , Resource person: Harrington Gibson Location: Gibbs-Morrison Cafe (Gibbs-Morrison Cultural Center) | 1823 Church Street, Evanston, IL, 60201 Description: In Debate, students learn to slow their thinking down just enough to make it sharp. This is not about arguing loudly or trying to win at all costs. It is about learning how to see an issue clearly, build a position with purpose, and communicate in a way that earns respect. Students engage real-world topics that connect to their lives—community, technology, culture—and practice organizing their thoughts, supporting ideas with evidence, and listening closely to understand different perspectives without losing their own voice. Each session blends reflection, skill-building, and live practice through structured debates and guided dialogue. Along the way, students strengthen their ability to think critically, speak confidently, and manage emotions under pressure. The environment is grounded in respect and accountability, where every voice matters and every idea must stand on reason. By the end, students carry more than debate skills—they carry a way of thinking and communicating that will serve them in school, work, and everyday life. Eligible for childcare tax credit.

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Monday, June 29 2026. Schedule: Every day, 9:00 AM - 4:00 PM , From June 29, 2026 until July 2, 2026 , Gibbs-Morrison Cafe , Resource person: Harrington Gibson Location: Gibbs-Morrison Cafe (Gibbs-Morrison Cultural Center) | 1823 Church Street, Evanston, IL, 60201 Description: Theater: Express Yourself: Acting FUNdamentals is an engaging, confidence-building theatre class that uses play, movement, voice, and storytelling to strengthen communication and self-expression skills. Through exciting theatre games, vocal warm-ups, and performance activities inspired by master practitioners including Viola Spolin, Kristin Linklater, Michael Shurtleff, Stanislavski, and others, students explore the foundational acting tools of body, voice, focus, and imagination. By the end of the program, students will feel more confident expressing themselves authentically, speak more clearly and audibly while strengthening the physical voice, connect emotion to vocal expression, and work more comfortably in groups with increased focus and collaboration, and have gained a mini-canon of classic poems and stories. Eligible for childcare tax credit.

name: Camp FLIGHT (Week 7:  Science Fair Tinkering)

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Monday, July 20 2026. Schedule: Every day, 9:00 AM - 4:00 PM , From July 20, 2026 until July 24, 2026 , Gibbs-Morrison Cafe , Resource person: Harrington Gibson Location: Gibbs-Morrison Cafe (Gibbs-Morrison Cultural Center) | 1823 Church Street, Evanston, IL, 60201 Description: Science Fair Tinkering – Go STEM For two weeks, Camp Flight is proud to partner with Go STEM Chicago to engage campers in a hands-on, inquiry-driven science fair experience. Through this partnership, students move beyond worksheets and simulations and into real investigation—asking questions, testing ideas, and building projects that reflect how science and problem-solving show up in the real world. Go STEM facilitators guide campers through the full science fair process: developing a question, conducting research, designing experiments, analyzing results, and preparing a clear, confident presentation of their findings. Students work independently and collaboratively, learning how to think critically, revise their ideas, and communicate their work to others. The two-week arc allows for depth rather than rush, reinforcing Camp Flight’s belief that sustained curiosity, thoughtful iteration, and public sharing are where real learning—and real confidence—take root. Eligible for childcare tax credit.

name: Camp FLIGHT (Week 9: Culinary)

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Monday, July 27 2026. Schedule: Every day, 9:00 AM - 4:00 PM , From July 27, 2026 until July 31, 2026 , Gibbs-Morrison Cafe , Resource person: Harrington Gibson Location: Gibbs-Morrison Cafe (Gibbs-Morrison Cultural Center) | 1823 Church Street, Evanston, IL, 60201 Description: Culinary Week invites Camp Flight participants into the practice of nourishment as both skill and responsibility. Students explore how to prepare simple, healthy meals while learning the foundations of nutrition, food safety, and kitchen confidence. A central thread of the experience is self-sufficiency—understanding how to select, prepare, and combine ingredients in ways that support the body and mind. Whenever possible, meals are created using what students have harvested themselves, connecting the full cycle from soil to plate. Beyond cooking, the week builds awareness and discipline. Participants begin to see how their food choices impact energy, focus, and overall well-being. They learn to plan, collaborate, and adapt, gaining practical life skills that extend far beyond the kitchen. Culinary Week becomes more than preparing meals—it is about cultivating independence, respect for resources, and the ability to sustain oneself with intention. Eligible for childcare tax credit.

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Saturday, May 23 2026. Schedule: Saturday, 7:00 PM - 9:00 PM , Noyes Street Theatre , Location: Noyes Street Theatre (Noyes Cultural Arts Center) | 927 Noyes Street, Evanston, IL, 60201 Description: Gee's Bend is the story of the Pettway women, quilters from the isolated community of Gee's Bend, Alabama. Beginning in 1939, the play follows Alice, her daughters Sadie and Nella, and Sadie's husband, Macon, through segregation, family strife, and the Civil Rights movement. Throughout their lives, the women's extraordinary quilts provide a respite from the turmoil around them. In the last act of the play, it is the year 2000; the quilts have been discovered as folk art and have become very valuable. Sadie is pleased with the recognition, but despite the lure of the big city, she returns to Gee's Bend and continues to quilt. Wilder's play explores the resilience of the human spirit, especially as it is expressed in art. No Transfer/Refunds

Beginning in 1939, the play follows Alice, her daughters Sadie and Nella, and Sadie's husband, Macon, through segregation, family strife, and the Civil Rights movement. Throughout their lives, the women's extraordinary quilts provide a respite from the turmoil around them. In the last act of the play, it is the year 2000; the quilts have been discovered as folk art and have become very valuable. Sadie is pleased with the recognition, but despite the lure of the big city, she returns to Gee's Bend and continues to quilt. Wilder's play explores the resilience of the human spirit, especially as it is expressed in art. No Transfers/Refunds
